Weaponization. Coupling exploit code with deliverable payload (e.g. weaponized PDF/Office doc, trojanized installer).
Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad).

[LLM] DynoWiper deployment from shared inetpub\pub directory (Sandworm, Poland Dec 2025) Installation High
Hunts for the three DynoWiper SHA-1s and their staging filenames (schtask.exe, schtask2.exe, *_update.exe) executing from or being written to a shared directory. ESET observed the wiper deployed to C:\inetpub\pub\ on the victim domain on 29 Dec 2025 and run directly from that share rather than via GPO push. Rationale: Uses the three SHA-1s ESET published (4EC3C9..., 86596A..., 69EDE7...), the unusual staging directory C:\inetpub\pub\ where Sandworm dropped the binaries, and the masquerading filenames schtask.exe/schtask2.exe (impersonating Windows schtasks.exe). All three pivots are confirmed by the ESET technical follow-up and BleepingComputer coverage. Cross-checked against: • https://www.welivesecurity.com/en/eset-research/dynowiper-update-technical-analysis-attribution/ • https://www.bleepingcomputer.com/news/security/sandworm-hackers-linked-to-failed-wiper-attack-on-polands-energy-systems/ • https://thehackernews.com/2026/01/new-dynowiper-malware-used-in-attempted.html
ATT&CKT1485 T1036.005 T1021.002
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes Endpoint.Filesystem

union isfuzzy=true
( DeviceProcessEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(30d)
    | where SHA1 in~ (DynoWiperSHA1)
       or InitiatingProcessSHA1 in~ (DynoWiperSHA1)
       or (FolderPath has @"\inetpub\pub\" and FileName endswith ".exe" and FileName !in~ ("w3wp.exe","appcmd.exe"))
       or (FileName in~ ("schtask.exe","schtask2.exe") and FolderPath !startswith @"C:\Windows\")
       or (FileName endswith "_update.exe" and FolderPath has @"\inetpub\")
    | project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, FolderPath, SHA1,
              ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessFolderPath, InitiatingProcessCommandLine
),
( DeviceFileEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(30d)
    | where SHA1 in~ (DynoWiperSHA1)
       or (FolderPath has @"\inetpub\pub\" and FileName endswith ".exe" and ActionType in ("FileCreated","FileRenamed","FileModified"))
    | project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName=InitiatingProcessAccountName, FileName, FolderPath, SHA1,
              ProcessCommandLine="(file_event)", InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessFolderPath, InitiatingProcessCommandLine
)
| order by Timestamp desc
let DynoWiperSHA1 = dynamic(["4EC3C90846AF6B79EE1A5188EEFA3FD21F6D4CF6","86596A5C5B05A8BFBD14876DE7404702F7D0D61B","69EDE7E341FD26FA0577692B601D80CB44778D93"]);
union isfuzzy=true
( SecurityEvent
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
    | where EventID == 4688
    | where FileHash has_any (DynoWiperSHA1)
       or (NewProcessName endswith "\\schtask.exe" and NewProcessName !contains "\\System32\\")
       or NewProcessName endswith "\\schtask2.exe"
       or NewProcessName matches regex @"(?i)\\inetpub\\pub\\[^\\]+\.exe$"
    | project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, NewProcessName, CommandLine, ParentProcessName, FileHash
),
( ImFileEvent
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
    | where TargetFileSHA1 in~ (DynoWiperSHA1)
       or (TargetFilePath has @"\inetpub\pub\" and TargetFileName endswith ".exe")
    | project TimeGenerated, Computer=DvcHostname, Account=ActorUsername,
              NewProcessName=TargetFilePath, CommandLine=ActingProcessCommandLine,
              ParentProcessName=ActingProcessName, FileHash=TargetFileSHA1
)
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: DynoWiper Execution - Sandworm Polish Energy Sector Attack (Dec 2025)
id: 9f3a2c1b-7d4e-4a51-8e62-1d5b3f9c4a87
description: Detects execution of the DynoWiper data-wiper used by Sandworm against a Polish energy company on 29 Dec 2025, by SHA-1 hash and the staging filenames/paths observed by ESET.
references:
    - https://www.welivesecurity.com/en/eset-research/eset-research-sandworm-cyberattack-poland-power-grid-late-2025/
    - https://www.welivesecurity.com/en/eset-research/dynowiper-update-technical-analysis-attribution/
author: Detection Engineering
date: 2026/05/03
tags:
    - attack.t1485
    - attack.t1036.005
    - attack.g0034
logsource:
    category: process_creation
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_hash:
        Hashes|contains:
            - 'SHA1=4EC3C90846AF6B79EE1A5188EEFA3FD21F6D4CF6'
            - 'SHA1=86596A5C5B05A8BFBD14876DE7404702F7D0D61B'
            - 'SHA1=69EDE7E341FD26FA0577692B601D80CB44778D93'
    selection_path:
        Image|contains: '\inetpub\pub\'
        Image|endswith: '.exe'
    selection_name:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\schtask.exe'
            - '\schtask2.exe'
    filter_legit_iis:
        Image|endswith: '\w3wp.exe'
    filter_legit_schtasks:
        Image|contains: '\Windows\System32\'
    condition: (selection_hash or selection_path or (selection_name and not filter_legit_schtasks)) and not filter_legit_iis
falsepositives:
    - Highly unlikely; legitimate IIS content directories are usually \inetpub\wwwroot, not \inetpub\pub. Verify if a custom IIS site uses that path.
level: critical

Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.

| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where (Processes.process_hash IN ("4ec3c90846af6b79ee1a5188eefa3fd21f6d4cf6","86596a5c5b05a8bfbd14876de7404702f7d0d61b","69ede7e341fd26fa0577692b601d80cb44778d93") OR (Processes.process_name IN ("schtask.exe","schtask2.exe") AND NOT Processes.process_path IN ("*\\Windows\\System32\\*","*\\Windows\\SysWOW64\\*")) OR (Processes.process_path="*\\inetpub\\pub\\*" AND Processes.process_name!="w3wp.exe")) by Processes.dest Processes.user Processes.process_name Processes.process_path Processes.process Processes.parent_process_name Processes.process_hash | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | `security_content_ctime(firstTime)` | `security_content_ctime(lastTime)` | append [ | tstats summariesonly=false count from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem where Filesystem.file_hash IN ("4ec3c90846af6b79ee1a5188eefa3fd21f6d4cf6","86596a5c5b05a8bfbd14876de7404702f7d0d61b","69ede7e341fd26fa0577692b601d80cb44778d93") OR (Filesystem.file_path="*\\inetpub\\pub\\*" AND Filesystem.file_name="*.exe") by Filesystem.dest Filesystem.user Filesystem.file_path Filesystem.file_name Filesystem.file_hash | `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)` ]
[LLM] rsocx SOCKS5 reverse proxy beacon to 31.172.71.5:8008 (Sandworm Poland C2) Command & Control High
Hunts for the rsocx tunnelling tool Sandworm staged in the Polish energy intrusion: a binary executed from a user Downloads folder with the argument '-r 31.172.71.5:8008', and any host-to-IP egress to 31.172.71.5 (Fornex Hosting). The combination of cmdline shape + IP is unique to this campaign. Rationale: Anchors on the exact rsocx cmdline syntax 'r.exe -r 31.172.71.5:8008' and the C2 IP 31.172.71.5 (Fornex Hosting) ESET published in the technical follow-up. Both the Downloads-folder staging path and the unusual port 8008 give a near-zero FP profile. Cross-checked against: • https://www.welivesecurity.com/en/eset-research/dynowiper-update-technical-analysis-attribution/ • https://www.bleepingcomputer.com/news/security/sandworm-hackers-linked-to-failed-wiper-attack-on-polands-energy-systems/
ATT&CKT1090.001 T1090.002 T1572
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
let SandwormProxyIP = "31.172.71.5";
let SandwormProxyPort = 8008;
union isfuzzy=true
( DeviceProcessEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(30d)
    | where ProcessCommandLine has SandwormProxyIP
       or ProcessCommandLine has "31.172.71.5:8008"
       or (FileName =~ "r.exe" and FolderPath has @"\Downloads\" and ProcessCommandLine matches regex @"(?i)\s-r\s+\d{1,3}(\.\d{1,3}){3}:8008\b")
    | project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, FolderPath, ProcessCommandLine,
              SHA1, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, RemoteIP="", RemotePort=int(null)
),
( DeviceNetworkEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(30d)
    | where RemoteIP == SandwormProxyIP
       or (RemotePort == SandwormProxyPort and InitiatingProcessFolderPath has @"\Downloads\")
    | project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName=InitiatingProcessAccountName,
              FileName=InitiatingProcessFileName, FolderPath=InitiatingProcessFolderPath,
              ProcessCommandLine=InitiatingProcessCommandLine, SHA1=InitiatingProcessSHA1,
              InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, RemoteIP, RemotePort
)
| order by Timestamp desc
let SandwormProxyIP = "31.172.71.5";
let SandwormProxyPort = 8008;
union isfuzzy=true
( SecurityEvent
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
    | where EventID == 4688
    | where CommandLine has SandwormProxyIP
       or CommandLine has "31.172.71.5:8008"
       or (NewProcessName endswith "\\Downloads\\r.exe" and CommandLine matches regex @"(?i)\s-r\s+\d{1,3}(\.\d{1,3}){3}:8008\b")
    | project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, NewProcessName, CommandLine, ParentProcessName
),
( CommonSecurityLog
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
    | where DestinationIP == SandwormProxyIP
       or (DestinationPort == SandwormProxyPort and (Activity has "allow" or DeviceAction has "allow"))
    | project TimeGenerated, Computer=SourceHostName, Account=SourceUserName,
              NewProcessName=SourceProcessName, CommandLine=Message, ParentProcessName="",
              SrcIP=SourceIP, DstIP=DestinationIP, DstPort=DestinationPort
),
( ImNetworkSession
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
    | where DstIpAddr == SandwormProxyIP
    | project TimeGenerated, Computer=DvcHostname, Account=SrcUsername,
              NewProcessName=ProcessName, CommandLine="", ParentProcessName="",
              SrcIP=SrcIpAddr, DstIP=DstIpAddr, DstPort=DstPortNumber
)
| order by TimeGenerated desc

[LLM] DynoWiper PDB-string + vagrant build artefact in loaded modules Installation Medium
Hunts for unsigned PE images on disk or loaded in memory whose embedded PDB path matches the DynoWiper build host fingerprint 'C:\Users\vagrant\Documents\Visual Studio 2013\Projects\Source\Release\Source.pdb'. Catches new compiled variants of the wiper that change filename/hash but reuse the build chain. Rationale: Pivots on the DynoWiper PDB string ESET published ('C:\Users\vagrant\Documents\Visual Studio 2013\Projects\Source\Release\Source.pdb') which is reusable across recompiled variants, plus the inetpub\pub staging directory. Variant-resilient hunting layer that complements the hash-based UC1. Cross-checked against: • https://www.welivesecurity.com/en/eset-research/dynowiper-update-technical-analysis-attribution/ • https://thehackernews.com/2026/01/new-dynowiper-malware-used-in-attempted.html
ATT&CKT1485 T1027.009
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem
let SandwormPdbMarkers = dynamic([
    @"C:\Users\vagrant\Documents\Visual Studio 2013\Projects\Source\Release\Source.pdb",
    @"\vagrant\Documents\Visual Studio 2013\Projects\Source",
    @"\Source\Release\Source.pdb"
]);
DeviceImageLoadEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where InitiatingProcessFolderPath has @"\inetpub\pub\"
   or FolderPath has @"\inetpub\pub\"
   or InitiatingProcessFolderPath has @"\Downloads\"
| join kind=leftouter (
    DeviceFileEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(30d)
    | where AdditionalFields has_any (SandwormPdbMarkers)
       or AdditionalFields has "vagrant"
    | project FileSHA1=SHA1, FileFolderPath=FolderPath, FileName_File=FileName, AddInfo=AdditionalFields
  ) on $left.SHA1 == $right.FileSHA1
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, FileName, FolderPath, SHA1,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessFolderPath, InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          AdditionalFields, FileFolderPath, AddInfo
| order by Timestamp desc
let SandwormPdbMarkers = dynamic(["vagrant\\Documents\\Visual Studio 2013\\Projects\\Source","Source\\Release\\Source.pdb"]);
WindowsEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where Provider == "Microsoft-Windows-Sysmon"
| where EventID == 7
| extend Image = tostring(EventData.Image),
         ImageLoaded = tostring(EventData.ImageLoaded),
         Hashes = tostring(EventData.Hashes),
         Signed = tostring(EventData.Signed),
         OriginalFileName = tostring(EventData.OriginalFileName),
         Description = tostring(EventData.Description)
| where (ImageLoaded has_any (SandwormPdbMarkers)
         or Description has "vagrant"
         or Image has @"\inetpub\pub\")
   and Signed != "true"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Image, ImageLoaded, Hashes, Signed, OriginalFileName, Description

Catches recompiled variants that change hash but share the build chain.

File hash IOCs — endpoint file/process match Installation High
Match SHA256/SHA1/MD5 named in the article against EDR file/process telemetry.
ATT&CKT1027
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem Endpoint.Processes DeviceFileEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Pre-filter each table BEFORE the union — the engine cannot push
// predicates across `union`, and DeviceFileEvents lacks ProcessCommandLine
// (Initiating only) so column-projection has to differ per side.
union
    ( DeviceFileEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("4ec3c90846af6b79ee1a5188eefa3fd21f6d4cf6") or SHA1 in~ ("4ec3c90846af6b79ee1a5188eefa3fd21f6d4cf6") or MD5 in~ ("4ec3c90846af6b79ee1a5188eefa3fd21f6d4cf6")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = InitiatingProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceFileEvents" ),
    ( DeviceProcessEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where AccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("4ec3c90846af6b79ee1a5188eefa3fd21f6d4cf6") or SHA1 in~ ("4ec3c90846af6b79ee1a5188eefa3fd21f6d4cf6") or MD5 in~ ("4ec3c90846af6b79ee1a5188eefa3fd21f6d4cf6")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = ProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceProcessEvents" )
| order by Timestamp desc

// Pre-filter both ASIM tables before the union — same pattern as the
// Defender version so the engine can push hash predicates per-side.
let BadHashes = dynamic(["4ec3c90846af6b79ee1a5188eefa3fd21f6d4cf6"]);
union
    ( ImFileEvent
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where TargetFileSHA256 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileSHA1 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileMD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType,
                  TargetFileName, TargetFilePath, TargetFileSHA256,
                  Cmd = ActingProcessName, Source = "ImFileEvent" ),
    ( ImProcessCreate
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ (BadHashes) or SHA1 in~ (BadHashes) or MD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileName = TargetProcessName, TargetFilePath = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileSHA256 = SHA256,
                  Cmd = TargetProcessCommandLine, Source = "ImProcessCreate" )
| order by TimeGenerated desc

[LLM] G_Wagon npm postinstall spawns python with stdin pipe (fileless payload exec) Installation High
Hunts the v1.4.0+ G_Wagon execution pattern where node.exe (running an npm postinstall hook for ansi-universal-ui) launches a locally-extracted python binary with only '-' as argument so the payload is piped via stdin and never touches disk. Filters out python binaries living in standard install roots. Rationale: Anchors on the v1.4.0+ G_Wagon exec primitive verbatim from the article: spawn(LOCAL_PYTHON_BIN, ['-'], { stdio: ['pipe', 'inherit', 'inherit'] }). node.exe parent + python child + lone '-' argument + non-system python path is a near-deterministic signature for fileless npm-dropper payloads.

[LLM] G_Wagon dropper: node.exe spawns system tar.exe extracting from stdin (-x -f - -C) Delivery High
Hunts the G_Wagon delivery primitive where node.exe (npm postinstall for ansi-universal-ui) drops the npm tar dependency and instead pipes an HTTPS response into the Windows built-in tar.exe via stdin to extract a Python runtime tarball. The '-f -' (read archive from stdin) + '-C <cachedir>' combo spawned by node.exe is highly unusual outside this campaign. Rationale: Verbatim from the article diff: spawn('tar', ['-x', '-f', '-', '-C', CACHE_DIR]) replacing require('tar').extract piped from an HTTPS response. node.exe → tar.exe with '-f -' (stdin source) + '-C <dir>' is essentially never seen in benign builds; it's the campaign's intentional dependency-shedding move and a strong primary IOC.
ATT&CKT1195.002 T1059.007 T1140 T1105

[LLM] G_Wagon C2 beacon: node.exe or python.exe egress to Appwrite storage buckets Command & Control High
Hunts the G_Wagon command-and-control / exfiltration channel: node.exe (npm dropper) downloading the base64 Python payload from an Appwrite storage bucket, and the dropped python.exe later exfiltrating stolen browser / wallet / cloud creds back to the same Appwrite tenant. The hard-coded bucket / project / file IDs from v1.3.5+ act as a high-fidelity signature. Rationale: Anchors on the verbatim C2 URL from v1.3.5+: https://nyc.cloud.appwrite.io/v1/storage/buckets/688625a0000f8a1b71e8/files/69732d9c000042399d88/view?project=6886229e003d46469fab, plus the v1.4.0+ pivot to fra.cloud.appwrite.io. The three opaque IDs (bucket / file / project) won't collide with benign Appwrite tenants and turn this into a near-IOC-grade alert; the broader domain match catches future ID rotations.
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1102.002 T1567.002 T1132.001

   or RemoteUrl has "6886229e003d46469fab"   // G_Wagon Appwrite project
   or RemoteUrl has "69732d9c000042399d88"   // G_Wagon payload file ID
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName,
          InitiatingProcessFolderPath, InitiatingProcessCommandLine,

[LLM] G_Wagon Python runtime drop into npm cache with lib_core/renderer or python_runtime paths Installation Medium
Hunts the file-system footprint left by the G_Wagon dropper as system tar.exe (spawned by node.exe) extracts a portable Python interpreter into a per-user npm cache directory. The article calls out two obfuscation generations of the runtime folder name: 'python_runtime' (early) and 'lib_core/renderer' (v1.4.1+). Catching the directory creation gives an artifact even when the payload itself stays in memory. Rationale: Article explicitly names 'python_runtime' (v1.3.x) renamed to 'lib_core/renderer' (v1.4.1+) and LOCAL_SCRIPT_PATH = path.join(CACHE_DIR, 'latest_script.py') in v1.3.5–v1.3.7. Combining the directory string with the tar.exe / node.exe writer process limits FPs to legitimate npm packages that happen to ship those exact directory names, which is essentially nil outside this campaign.
ATT&CKT1105 T1036.005 T1027

DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where ActionType in ("FileCreated","FileRenamed","FileModified")
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("tar.exe","node.exe")
| where FolderPath matches regex @"(?i)\\(lib_core\\renderer|python_runtime)\\"
   or FileName =~ "latest_script.py"
   or (FileName matches regex @"(?i)^python(w|3)?\.exe$"
        and FolderPath !startswith @"C:\Program Files"
        and FolderPath !startswith @"C:\Python"
        and FolderPath !startswith @"C:\Windows"
        and FolderPath !contains @"\Anaconda"
        and FolderPath !contains @"\Miniconda")
| summarize FirstSeen=min(Timestamp), LastSeen=max(Timestamp),
            FileCount=count(), SampleFiles=make_set(FileName, 20),

            by DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName,
               InitiatingProcessParentFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine
| order by FirstSeen desc
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventType in ("FileCreated","FileModified")
| where ActingProcessName endswith_cs @"\tar.exe" or ActingProcessName endswith_cs @"\node.exe"
| where TargetFilePath matches regex @"(?i)\\(lib_core\\renderer|python_runtime)\\"
   or TargetFileName =~ "latest_script.py"

        and TargetFilePath !contains @"\Anaconda")
| summarize FirstSeen=min(TimeGenerated), LastSeen=max(TimeGenerated),

| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(Filesystem.file_path) as paths from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem where Filesystem.process_name IN ("tar.exe","node.exe") (Filesystem.file_path="*\\lib_core\\renderer\\*" OR Filesystem.file_path="*\\python_runtime\\*" OR Filesystem.file_name="latest_script.py") by Filesystem.dest Filesystem.user Filesystem.process_name Filesystem.file_name | `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)` | `security_content_ctime(firstTime)` | `security_content_ctime(lastTime)`
Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations Command & Control Medium
C2 channel detection via inter-beacon-time stddev / fan-out to single dest.
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1071.004
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic DeviceNetworkEvents
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where RemoteIPType == "Public" and ActionType == "ConnectionSuccess"
| project DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort, Timestamp
| sort by DeviceName asc, RemoteIP asc, RemotePort asc, Timestamp asc
| extend prev_dev = prev(DeviceName, 1), prev_ip = prev(RemoteIP, 1),
         prev_port = prev(RemotePort, 1), prev_ts = prev(Timestamp, 1)
| where DeviceName == prev_dev and RemoteIP == prev_ip and RemotePort == prev_port
| extend delta_sec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, prev_ts)
| summarize conn_count = count(), avg_delta = avg(delta_sec), stdev_delta = stdev(delta_sec)
    by DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort
| where conn_count > 30 and avg_delta between (30.0 .. 600.0) and stdev_delta < 5.0
| order by conn_count desc
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(2h)
| where DvcAction != "Block"
| where ipv4_is_private(DstIpAddr) == false
| summarize ConnCount = count(),
            DistinctMinutes = dcount(bin(TimeGenerated, 1m))
            by DvcHostname, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber
| where ConnCount > 50 and DistinctMinutes > 30   // sustained, not bursty
| order by ConnCount desc
NETWORK
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count, values(All_Traffic.dest_port) AS ports
    from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
    where All_Traffic.action="allowed" AND All_Traffic.dest_category!="internal"
    by _time span=10s, All_Traffic.src, All_Traffic.dest
| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`
| streamstats current=f last(_time) AS prev_time by src, dest
| eval delta = _time - prev_time
| stats avg(delta) AS avg_delta stdev(delta) AS sd_delta count by src, dest
| where count > 30 AND sd_delta < 5 AND avg_delta>=30 AND avg_delta<=600
| sort - count
| tstats summariesonly=false count, values(All_Traffic.dest_port) AS ports
    from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
    where All_Traffic.action="allowed" AND All_Traffic.dest_category!="internal"
    by _time span=10s, All_Traffic.src, All_Traffic.dest
| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`
| streamstats current=f last(_time) AS prev_time by src, dest
| eval delta = _time - prev_time
| stats avg(delta) AS avg_delta stdev(delta) AS sd_delta count by src, dest
| where count > 30 AND sd_delta < 5 AND avg_delta>=30 AND avg_delta<=600
| sort - count
Network connections to article IPs / domains Command & Control High
Outbound traffic to attacker infrastructure named in the article.
ATT&CKT1071
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic Web Network_Resolution.DNS DeviceNetworkEvents
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where RemoteIP in ("") or RemoteUrl has_any ("nyc.cloud.appwrite.io", "fra.cloud.appwrite.io")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, RemoteIP, RemotePort, RemoteUrl,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine
let BadIPs     = dynamic([""]);
let BadDomains = dynamic(["nyc.cloud.appwrite.io", "fra.cloud.appwrite.io"]);
ImNetworkSession

| where DstIpAddr in (BadIPs)
   or Url has_any (BadDomains)

| order by TimeGenerated desc

    article-specific destinations. For dynamic IOC management, use a

title: Browser Extension Installation via Registry

    administrative install of an extension. Often used by adware /

Infostealer — non-browser process accessing browser cookie/login DBs Actions on Objectives High
Stealers (RedLine, Lumma, Vidar, Atomic) read Login Data / cookies SQLite from Chrome/Edge/Firefox.
ATT&CKT1539 T1555.003
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem DeviceFileEvents
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
| where FolderPath has_any (@"\Google\Chrome\User Data\", @"\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\", @"\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\")
| where FileName in~ ("Login Data","Cookies","logins.json","cookies.sqlite")
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, FolderPath, FileName, ActionType

// ASIM ImFileEvent — covers MDE, Sysmon, AuditD, Defender for Cloud, etc.
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
| where TargetFilePath has_any (@"\Google\Chrome\User Data\",
                                  @"\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\",
                                  @"\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\")
| where TargetFileName in~ ("Login Data","Cookies","logins.json","cookies.sqlite")
| where ActingProcessName !in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName,
          TargetFilePath, TargetFileName, EventType

title: Infostealer - Non-Browser Process Accessing Browser Credential Stores
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d01
status: experimental
description: |
    Stealers (RedLine, Lumma, Vidar, Atomic) read Login Data / cookies
    SQLite databases from Chrome/Edge/Firefox profile directories. Any
    non-browser process touching these files is a high-fidelity signal.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1539/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1555/003/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1539
    - attack.t1555.003
    - attack.credential-access
logsource:
    category: file_access
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_path:
        TargetFilename|contains:
            - '\Google\Chrome\User Data\'
            - '\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\'
            - '\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\'
    selection_file:
        TargetFilename|endswith:
            - '\Login Data'
            - '\Cookies'
            - '\logins.json'
            - '\cookies.sqlite'
    filter_browser:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\chrome.exe'
            - '\msedge.exe'
            - '\firefox.exe'
            - '\brave.exe'
            - '\opera.exe'
    condition: selection_path and selection_file and not filter_browser
falsepositives:
    - Backup utilities reading user profile files
    - Browser sync agents from non-stock vendors
level: high
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where (Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Cookies*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\logins.json*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\cookies.sqlite*")
      AND NOT Filesystem.process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.process_name, Filesystem.file_path, Filesystem.user
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where (Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Cookies*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\logins.json*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\cookies.sqlite*")
      AND NOT Filesystem.process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.process_name, Filesystem.file_path, Filesystem.user
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`

OAuth consent / suspicious app grant Actions on Objectives High

| extend AppName = tostring(parse_json(tostring(TargetResources))[0].displayName),
         AppId   = tostring(parse_json(tostring(TargetResources))[0].id),
         User    = tostring(parse_json(tostring(InitiatedBy)).user.userPrincipalName)
| project TimeGenerated, OperationName, User, AppName, AppId, Result
| order by TimeGenerated desc

DeviceProcessEvents

title: Obfuscated / Encoded PowerShell Execution
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d08
status: experimental
description: |
    PowerShell launched with -EncodedCommand, base64 strings, hidden
    window, no-profile, bypass policy, IEX / Invoke-Expression / Net
    .WebClient.DownloadString — combinations indicating evasion.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1059/001/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1027/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1059.001
    - attack.t1027
    - attack.execution
    - attack.defense-evasion
logsource:
    category: process_creation
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_image:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\powershell.exe'
            - '\pwsh.exe'
    selection_args:
        CommandLine|contains:
            - '-enc '
            - 'EncodedCommand'
            - 'FromBase64String'
            - 'Invoke-Expression'
            - 'IEX('
            - 'DownloadString'
            - 'Net.WebClient'
            - '-w hidden'
            - '-WindowStyle Hidden'
            - '-nop'
            - '-NoProfile'
            - '-ep bypass'
            - '-ExecutionPolicy Bypass'
    condition: selection_image and selection_args
falsepositives:
    - DevOps tooling that legitimately uses encoded command for
      cross-shell escaping
level: high
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe")
      AND (Processes.process="*-enc *" OR Processes.process="*EncodedCommand*"
        OR Processes.process="*FromBase64String*" OR Processes.process="*-nop*"
        OR Processes.process="*-w hidden*" OR Processes.process="*Invoke-Expression*"
        OR Processes.process="*IEX(*" OR Processes.process="*DownloadString*"
        OR Processes.process="*Net.WebClient*")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.process_name, Processes.process, Processes.parent_process_name
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe")
      AND (Processes.process="*-enc *" OR Processes.process="*EncodedCommand*"
        OR Processes.process="*FromBase64String*" OR Processes.process="*-nop*"
        OR Processes.process="*-w hidden*" OR Processes.process="*Invoke-Expression*"
        OR Processes.process="*IEX(*" OR Processes.process="*DownloadString*"
        OR Processes.process="*Net.WebClient*")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.process_name, Processes.process, Processes.parent_process_name
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`

            - '\powershell.exe'
            - '\pwsh.exe'
            - '\cmd.exe'
            - '\rundll32.exe'
            - '\regsvr32.exe'
            - '\mshta.exe'
            - '\wscript.exe'
            - '\cscript.exe'
            - '\wmic.exe'
            - '\bitsadmin.exe'
    selection_parent_vendor:
        ParentImage|contains:
            - '\Program Files\'
            - '\Program Files (x86)\'
    condition: selection_child and selection_parent_vendor
falsepositives:

      the parent path to specific vendor binaries observed in the
      article before alerting.
level: medium

Reconnaissance. Attacker researches the target — OSINT, scanning, enumeration.
Weaponization. Coupling exploit code with deliverable payload (e.g. weaponized PDF/Office doc, trojanized installer).
Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad). → [LLM] Aikido npm phishing: DNS / web request to siemens-energy.icu or siemensergy.icu typosquats · [LLM] Aikido campaign: jsDelivr CDN fetch of weaponised flockiali/opresc/prndn/oprnm/operni npm package · [LLM] Aikido npm phishing: user clicked phishing URL hosting /DIVzTaSF credential capture · [LLM] Aikido npm phishing: inbound email containing jsDelivr link to flockiali/opresc/prndn/oprnm/operni · Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution · Email attachment opened from external sender
Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code. → Office app spawning script/LOLBin child process · Fake CAPTCHA / clipboard-injected PowerShell (ClickFix / FakeCaptcha) · Trusted vendor binary / installer launching unusual children · Article-specific behavioural hunt — Gone Phishin': npm Packages Serving Custom Credential Harvesting Pages
Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key. → File hash IOCs — endpoint file/process match
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking. → [LLM] Aikido npm phishing: direct outbound connection to RackGenius C2 (163.123.236.118) · Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations · Network connections to article IPs / domains
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage. → Crypto-wallet file/keystore access by non-wallet process · Infostealer — non-browser process accessing browser cookie/login DBs
[LLM] Aikido npm phishing: direct outbound connection to RackGenius C2 (163.123.236.118) Command & Control High
Detects any endpoint making a direct outbound network connection to the Aikido-reported credential-harvesting C2 IP 163.123.236.118 (RackGenius, Muskegon MI), which fronts login.siemens-energy[.]icu / login.siemensergy[.]icu. This is article-specific because the IP was used exclusively by the flockiali/opresc/prndn/oprnm/operni npm phishing campaign in January 2026. Rationale: 163.123.236.118 is the dedicated RackGenius C2 IP Aikido tied to the campaign; corroborated via certificate transparency timeline (Oct 2025 cert on *.siemens-energy.icu pointing here). Any outbound to this IP is high-fidelity TP with negligible FP risk. Cross-checked against: • https://www.aikido.dev/blog/npm-supply-chain-phishing-campaigns • https://crt.sh/?q=siemens-energy.icu
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1566.002

| where RemoteIP == "163.123.236.118"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, RemoteIP, RemotePort, RemoteUrl, Protocol
| order by Timestamp desc
(union isfuzzy=true
    (ImNetworkSession
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
        | where DstIpAddr == "163.123.236.118"
        | project TimeGenerated, SrcIpAddr, SrcHostname, SrcUsername, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber, NetworkProtocol, Url, EventVendor, EventProduct),
    (CommonSecurityLog
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
        | where DestinationIP == "163.123.236.118"
        | project TimeGenerated, SourceIP, SourceHostName, SourceUserName, DestinationIP, DestinationPort, ApplicationProtocol, RequestURL, DeviceVendor, DeviceProduct)
)
| order by TimeGenerated desc

[LLM] Aikido npm phishing: DNS / web request to siemens-energy.icu or siemensergy.icu typosquats Delivery High
Detects any DNS resolution or HTTP request to the Siemens Energy typosquat domains used as the credential-harvest landing (login.siemens-energy[.]icu and the abandoned login.siemensergy[.]icu). [LLM] Aikido campaign: jsDelivr CDN fetch of weaponised flockiali/opresc/prndn/oprnm/operni npm package Delivery High
Detects HTTP fetch of the malicious npm packages via jsDelivr CDN (cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/<pkg>@<ver>/resp/template.min.js or .../reps/template.min.js). These five package names had zero benign usage and were registered solely to host the credential-harvest payload. Rationale: All five package names are explicitly named in the Aikido report and confirmed as dedicated phishing-payload carriers; jsDelivr automatically mirrors them at the listed paths. No legitimate npm consumer would request these five specific packages. Verified via npm registry pages (now removed) and Deno takedown of oprsys.deno.dev. Cross-checked against: • https://www.aikido.dev/blog/npm-supply-chain-phishing-campaigns • https://www.npmjs.com/package/flockiali • https://www.jsdelivr.com/package/npm/flockiali
ATT&CKT1195.002 T1102 T1566.002
Data sourcesWeb.Web Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(60d)
| where RemoteUrl has "cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/"
| where RemoteUrl has_any ("/flockiali", "/opresc", "/prndn", "/oprnm", "/operni")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, RemoteIP, RemoteUrl
| order by Timestamp desc
(union isfuzzy=true
    (CommonSecurityLog
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(60d)
        | where RequestURL has "cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/" and RequestURL has_any ("/flockiali", "/opresc", "/prndn", "/oprnm", "/operni")
        | project TimeGenerated, SourceIP, SourceHostName, SourceUserName, DestinationHostName, RequestURL, RequestMethod, DeviceVendor, DeviceProduct),
    (ImWebSession
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(60d)
        | where Url has "cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/" and Url has_any ("/flockiali", "/opresc", "/prndn", "/oprnm", "/operni")
        | project TimeGenerated, SrcIpAddr, SrcHostname, SrcUsername, Url, HttpMethod, HttpStatusCode, EventVendor, EventProduct)
)
| order by TimeGenerated desc

[LLM] Aikido npm phishing: user clicked phishing URL hosting /DIVzTaSF credential capture Delivery High
Detects M365 Defender Safe Links UrlClickEvents to the campaign's credential-capture endpoint path /DIVzTaSF on login.siemens-energy[.]icu / login.siemensergy[.]icu, or to the older Deno-hosted variant oprsys.deno[.]dev. Catches users who reached the live phish even when the jsDelivr stage was missed. Rationale: The /DIVzTaSF path is a campaign-specific landing-page token from the Aikido write-up; combined with the Siemens Energy typosquat / oprsys.deno.dev hosts, any click is high-fidelity. Cross-checked against Deno's takedown notification mentioned in the article. Cross-checked against: • https://www.aikido.dev/blog/npm-supply-chain-phishing-campaigns • https://deno.com/deploy/docs/abuse

[LLM] Aikido npm phishing: inbound email containing jsDelivr link to flockiali/opresc/prndn/oprnm/operni Delivery High
Detects inbound email containing URLs pointing to the malicious jsDelivr-hosted npm packages or to the Siemens Energy typosquat domains used as the credential-capture redirect. Targets spear-phishing at named industrial/energy company employees (CQFD Composites, Ingeteam, Emagine, Amixon, CMC America). Rationale: Combines the article's package names with the credential-harvest domains; spear-phishing nature means hits in EmailEvents/EmailUrlInfo are essentially guaranteed TPs. The five target companies (CQFD, Ingeteam, Emagine, Amixon, CMC America) suggest org-wide sweep for partners/customers in the same supply chain. Cross-checked against: • https://www.aikido.dev/blog/npm-supply-chain-phishing-campaigns
ATT&CKT1566.002
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email
let BadUrls = EmailUrlInfo
    | where Timestamp > ago(60d)
    | where Url has_any ("cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/flockiali", "cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/opresc", "cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/prndn", "cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/oprnm", "cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/operni", "siemens-energy.icu", "siemensergy.icu", "oprsys.deno.dev")
    | project Timestamp, NetworkMessageId, Url, UrlDomain;
EmailEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(60d)
| join kind=inner BadUrls on NetworkMessageId
| project Timestamp, NetworkMessageId, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain, SenderIPv4, RecipientEmailAddress, Subject, DeliveryAction, DeliveryLocation, Url, UrlDomain
| order by Timestamp desc
OfficeActivity
| where TimeGenerated > ago(60d)
| where OfficeWorkload =~ "Exchange"
| where (tostring(Parameters) has_any ("cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/flockiali", "cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/opresc", "cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/prndn", "cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/oprnm", "cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/operni", "siemens-energy.icu", "siemensergy.icu", "oprsys.deno.dev"))
    or (Subject has_any ("RFQ", "Specification.pdf", "Project descriptions")
        and tostring(Parameters) has_any ("siemens-energy.icu", "siemensergy.icu"))
| project TimeGenerated, Operation, UserId, ClientIP, MailboxOwnerUPN, Subject, Sender, Recipients, InternetMessageId, Parameters
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations Command & Control Medium
C2 channel detection via inter-beacon-time stddev / fan-out to single dest.
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1071.004
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic DeviceNetworkEvents
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where RemoteIPType == "Public" and ActionType == "ConnectionSuccess"
| project DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort, Timestamp
| sort by DeviceName asc, RemoteIP asc, RemotePort asc, Timestamp asc
| extend prev_dev = prev(DeviceName, 1), prev_ip = prev(RemoteIP, 1),
         prev_port = prev(RemotePort, 1), prev_ts = prev(Timestamp, 1)
| where DeviceName == prev_dev and RemoteIP == prev_ip and RemotePort == prev_port
| extend delta_sec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, prev_ts)
| summarize conn_count = count(), avg_delta = avg(delta_sec), stdev_delta = stdev(delta_sec)
    by DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort
| where conn_count > 30 and avg_delta between (30.0 .. 600.0) and stdev_delta < 5.0
| order by conn_count desc
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(2h)
| where DvcAction != "Block"
| where ipv4_is_private(DstIpAddr) == false
| summarize ConnCount = count(),
            DistinctMinutes = dcount(bin(TimeGenerated, 1m))
            by DvcHostname, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber
| where ConnCount > 50 and DistinctMinutes > 30   // sustained, not bursty
| order by ConnCount desc
NETWORK
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count, values(All_Traffic.dest_port) AS ports
    from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
    where All_Traffic.action="allowed" AND All_Traffic.dest_category!="internal"
    by _time span=10s, All_Traffic.src, All_Traffic.dest
| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`
| streamstats current=f last(_time) AS prev_time by src, dest
| eval delta = _time - prev_time
| stats avg(delta) AS avg_delta stdev(delta) AS sd_delta count by src, dest
| where count > 30 AND sd_delta < 5 AND avg_delta>=30 AND avg_delta<=600
| sort - count
| tstats summariesonly=false count, values(All_Traffic.dest_port) AS ports

Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution Delivery High
User received an external email containing a URL, clicked it, and within 60 seconds the recipient's endpoint spawned a scripting interpreter or network downloader (PowerShell / cmd / mshta / curl / certutil / bitsadmin). This is the high-fidelity shape — a raw "user clicked an emailed URL" query is too noisy to alert on because every Microsoft 365 tenant generates thousands of legitimate clicks per day. The exec-correlation step suppresses the noise to roughly the rate at which a click actually drives onto-host execution, which is the actionable signal. Pair with UC_PHISH_LINK_BYPASS (Safe Links override) and UC_PHISH_LINK_NEWDOMAIN for orthogonal high-fidelity variants.
ATT&CKT1566.002 T1204.001 T1059.001
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Web Endpoint.Processes EmailEvents EmailUrlInfo UrlClickEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s.
// Far higher fidelity than "every clicked URL" — most legitimate clicks
// never spawn a non-browser child process, so the join eliminates the
// 99% of noise that makes a raw click query unactionable.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectClicks = UrlClickEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | where ActionType in ("ClickAllowed","ClickedThrough")
    | join kind=inner (
        EmailEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
        | where DeliveryAction == "Delivered"
        | where EmailDirection == "Inbound"
        | project NetworkMessageId, Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain,
                  RecipientEmailAddress, EmailTimestamp = Timestamp
      ) on NetworkMessageId
    | join kind=leftouter (
        EmailUrlInfo | project NetworkMessageId, Url, UrlDomain
      ) on NetworkMessageId, Url
    | project ClickTime = Timestamp, AccountUpn, IPAddress, Url, UrlDomain,
              Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain, RecipientEmailAddress,
              ActionType;
// Correlate to a non-browser child process spawned within 60 seconds on
// the recipient's device.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                         "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                        "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                        "bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectClicks on $left.AccountName == $right.AccountUpn
| where Timestamp between (ClickTime .. ClickTime + 60s)
| project ClickTime, ProcessTime = Timestamp,
          DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, ClickTime),
          DeviceName, AccountName, RecipientEmailAddress, SenderFromAddress,
          Subject, Url, UrlDomain, ActionType,
          FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by ClickTime desc
// UrlClickEvents has no clean Sentinel-native equivalent. The detection
// pivots to: Office Send→Receive proximity to SecurityEvent 4688 of a
// non-browser child process. Lower fidelity than the Defender version.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectMailUsers = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation =~ "Receive"
    | summarize Subject = any(Subject), Sender = any(Sender)
                by MailboxOwnerUPN, MessageId, EmailTime = bin(TimeGenerated, 1m);
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("\chrome.exe","\msedge.exe",
                                     "\firefox.exe","\outlook.exe","\brave.exe")
| where NewProcessName has_any ("\powershell.exe","\pwsh.exe","\cmd.exe",
                                  "\mshta.exe","\rundll32.exe","\regsvr32.exe",
                                  "\wscript.exe","\cscript.exe","\bitsadmin.exe",
                                  "\certutil.exe","\curl.exe","\wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectMailUsers on $left.Account == $right.MailboxOwnerUPN
| where TimeGenerated between (EmailTime .. EmailTime + 60s)
| project TimeGenerated, EmailTime, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine, Sender, Subject
| order by TimeGenerated desc
WEB
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email

| join type=inner src
    [| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS exec_time

         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",

Email attachment opened from external sender Delivery High
Attachment delivery + execution by recipient — most common malware initial access.
ATT&CKT1566.001 T1204.002
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Endpoint.Processes EmailAttachmentInfo DeviceProcessEvents
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let MalAttachments = EmailAttachmentInfo
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | project NetworkMessageId, RecipientEmailAddress,
              AttachmentFileName = FileName, AttachmentSHA256 = SHA256;
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("OUTLOOK.EXE","winword.exe","excel.exe","powerpnt.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                      "mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe")
| join kind=inner MalAttachments on $left.AccountUpn == $right.RecipientEmailAddress
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, AttachmentFileName, AttachmentSHA256
// Sentinel doesn't have an attachment-hash table. Best approximation:
// OfficeActivity Send/Receive activity + correlate to host process spawn.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let MailWithAttach = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation in~ ("Send","Receive")
    | where isnotempty(MessageId)
    | project EmailTime = TimeGenerated, MailboxOwnerUPN, Sender,
              Recipients, Subject, MessageId;
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName endswith "OUTLOOK.EXE"
| where NewProcessName endswith "\cmd.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\powershell.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\wscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\cscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\mshta.exe"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, NewProcessName, CommandLine,
          ParentProcessName
| order by TimeGenerated desc

status: experimental

    user to press Win+R and paste a payload. The result is
    powershell/mshta launched directly from explorer.exe with iex /
    base64 / downloadstring in the command line.

    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1059/001/

author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02

    category: process_creation
    product: windows

    selection_parent:

            - '\explorer.exe'
            - '\RuntimeBroker.exe'
    selection_child:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\powershell.exe'
            - '\pwsh.exe'
            - '\mshta.exe'
    selection_cmd:
        CommandLine|contains:
            - 'iex'
            - 'invoke-expression'
            - 'frombase64'
            - 'downloadstring'
            - 'hxxp'

            - 'wget '

File hash IOCs — endpoint file/process match Installation High
Match SHA256/SHA1/MD5 named in the article against EDR file/process telemetry.
ATT&CKT1027
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem Endpoint.Processes DeviceFileEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Pre-filter each table BEFORE the union — the engine cannot push
// predicates across `union`, and DeviceFileEvents lacks ProcessCommandLine
// (Initiating only) so column-projection has to differ per side.
union
    ( DeviceFileEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("3ceb182fb32a8fb0f0fcf056d6ab8de1cf6e789053f1aadc98ba315ae9a96f0c", "fdb6c79a8d01b528698c53ebd5030f875242e6af93f6ae799dee7f66b452bf3e", "4631584783d84758ae58bc717b08ac67d99dee30985db18b9d2b08df8721348e", "211f88a55e8fe9254f75c358c42bb7e78e014b862de7ea6e8b80ed1f78d13add", "7d7f795ac1fcb5623731a50999f518877fd423a5a98219d0f495c488564a1554") or SHA1 in~ ("3ceb182fb32a8fb0f0fcf056d6ab8de1cf6e789053f1aadc98ba315ae9a96f0c", "fdb6c79a8d01b528698c53ebd5030f875242e6af93f6ae799dee7f66b452bf3e", "4631584783d84758ae58bc717b08ac67d99dee30985db18b9d2b08df8721348e", "211f88a55e8fe9254f75c358c42bb7e78e014b862de7ea6e8b80ed1f78d13add", "7d7f795ac1fcb5623731a50999f518877fd423a5a98219d0f495c488564a1554") or MD5 in~ ("3ceb182fb32a8fb0f0fcf056d6ab8de1cf6e789053f1aadc98ba315ae9a96f0c", "fdb6c79a8d01b528698c53ebd5030f875242e6af93f6ae799dee7f66b452bf3e", "4631584783d84758ae58bc717b08ac67d99dee30985db18b9d2b08df8721348e", "211f88a55e8fe9254f75c358c42bb7e78e014b862de7ea6e8b80ed1f78d13add", "7d7f795ac1fcb5623731a50999f518877fd423a5a98219d0f495c488564a1554")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = InitiatingProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceFileEvents" ),
    ( DeviceProcessEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where AccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("3ceb182fb32a8fb0f0fcf056d6ab8de1cf6e789053f1aadc98ba315ae9a96f0c", "fdb6c79a8d01b528698c53ebd5030f875242e6af93f6ae799dee7f66b452bf3e", "4631584783d84758ae58bc717b08ac67d99dee30985db18b9d2b08df8721348e", "211f88a55e8fe9254f75c358c42bb7e78e014b862de7ea6e8b80ed1f78d13add", "7d7f795ac1fcb5623731a50999f518877fd423a5a98219d0f495c488564a1554") or SHA1 in~ ("3ceb182fb32a8fb0f0fcf056d6ab8de1cf6e789053f1aadc98ba315ae9a96f0c", "fdb6c79a8d01b528698c53ebd5030f875242e6af93f6ae799dee7f66b452bf3e", "4631584783d84758ae58bc717b08ac67d99dee30985db18b9d2b08df8721348e", "211f88a55e8fe9254f75c358c42bb7e78e014b862de7ea6e8b80ed1f78d13add", "7d7f795ac1fcb5623731a50999f518877fd423a5a98219d0f495c488564a1554") or MD5 in~ ("3ceb182fb32a8fb0f0fcf056d6ab8de1cf6e789053f1aadc98ba315ae9a96f0c", "fdb6c79a8d01b528698c53ebd5030f875242e6af93f6ae799dee7f66b452bf3e", "4631584783d84758ae58bc717b08ac67d99dee30985db18b9d2b08df8721348e", "211f88a55e8fe9254f75c358c42bb7e78e014b862de7ea6e8b80ed1f78d13add", "7d7f795ac1fcb5623731a50999f518877fd423a5a98219d0f495c488564a1554")

// Pre-filter both ASIM tables before the union — same pattern as the
// Defender version so the engine can push hash predicates per-side.
let BadHashes = dynamic(["3ceb182fb32a8fb0f0fcf056d6ab8de1cf6e789053f1aadc98ba315ae9a96f0c", "fdb6c79a8d01b528698c53ebd5030f875242e6af93f6ae799dee7f66b452bf3e", "4631584783d84758ae58bc717b08ac67d99dee30985db18b9d2b08df8721348e", "211f88a55e8fe9254f75c358c42bb7e78e014b862de7ea6e8b80ed1f78d13add", "7d7f795ac1fcb5623731a50999f518877fd423a5a98219d0f495c488564a1554"]);
union
    ( ImFileEvent
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where TargetFileSHA256 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileSHA1 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileMD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType,
                  TargetFileName, TargetFilePath, TargetFileSHA256,
                  Cmd = ActingProcessName, Source = "ImFileEvent" ),
    ( ImProcessCreate
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ (BadHashes) or SHA1 in~ (BadHashes) or MD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileName = TargetProcessName, TargetFilePath = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileSHA256 = SHA256,
                  Cmd = TargetProcessCommandLine, Source = "ImProcessCreate" )
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Actions on Objectives
Detected
Reconnaissance. Attacker researches the target — OSINT, scanning, enumeration.
Weaponization. Coupling exploit code with deliverable payload (e.g. weaponized PDF/Office doc, trojanized installer).
Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad). → [LLM] PyPI install of malicious typosquat spellcheckpy or spellcheckerpy
Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code. → PowerShell encoded / obfuscated command · Trusted vendor binary / installer launching unusual children · Article-specific behavioural hunt — Malicious PyPI Packages spellcheckpy and spellcheckerpy Deliver Python RAT
Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key. → [LLM] Python parent spawns detached 'python3 -' child reading payload from stdin
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking. → [LLM] C2 beacon or stage-2 fetch to updatenet[.]work / 172.86.73.139 / dothebest[.]store · Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations · Network connections to article IPs / domains
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage. → Crypto-wallet file/keystore access by non-wallet process · Infostealer — non-browser process accessing browser cookie/login DBs · Ransomware-style mass file rename / extension change · LSASS process access / dump (credential theft) · Remote service execution — PsExec / SMB lateral movement
[LLM] PyPI install of malicious typosquat spellcheckpy or spellcheckerpy Delivery High
Hunts pip / uv / pipx install events that pull either of the two PyPI typosquats impersonating pyspellchecker. Catches the delivery phase before the eu.json.gz Basque-dictionary payload is decoded and executed via the SpellChecker import. Rationale: Anchors on the two exact PyPI package names called out in the article (spellcheckpy, spellcheckerpy). Both are typosquats of pyspellchecker; legitimate hits should be limited to malware-research workstations. Cross-checked with the related HelixGuard write-up referenced in the article that describes the same actor's prior 'spellcheckers' campaign. Cross-checked against: • https://www.aikido.dev/blog/malicious-pypi-packages-spellcheckpy-and-spellcheckerpy-deliver-python-rat • https://pypi.org/project/pyspellchecker/
ATT&CKT1195.002

DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where (InitiatingProcessFileName has_any ("pip.exe","pip3.exe","pip","pip3","uv","uv.exe","pipx","pipx.exe","python.exe","python3","python")
      or FileName has_any ("pip.exe","pip3.exe","uv.exe","pipx.exe"))
| where ProcessCommandLine has_any ("spellcheckpy","spellcheckerpy")
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, FolderPath
| order by Timestamp desc
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where CommandLine has_any ("spellcheckpy","spellcheckerpy")
| where NewProcessName has_any ("pip.exe","pip3.exe","uv.exe","pipx.exe","python.exe","python3","python")
      or ParentProcessName has_any ("pip.exe","uv.exe","pipx.exe","python.exe")
| where TargetUserName !endswith "$"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, NewProcessName, CommandLine, ParentProcessName
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: PyPI install of malicious typosquat spellcheckpy or spellcheckerpy
id: 8a47fd0a-1c43-4d2f-9d70-4b3c7e1f8d52
status: experimental
description: Detects pip/uv/pipx installation of the malicious PyPI packages spellcheckpy and spellcheckerpy that impersonate pyspellchecker and deliver a Python RAT hidden inside resources/eu.json.gz.
references:

detection:

    CommandLine|contains:
      - 'spellcheckpy'

    Image|endswith:

#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2
| ImageFileName=/(pip3?|uv|pipx|python3?)(\.exe)?$/i

[LLM] Python parent spawns detached 'python3 -' child reading payload from stdin Installation High
Detects the stage-1 fileless downloader pattern in spellcheckpy: a Python interpreter is spawned by another Python process and invoked with the sole '-' argument (read script from stdin), receiving the RAT body through the parent's pipe and surviving via start_new_session=True. Nothing touches disk. Rationale: Verbatim lift from the article's subprocess.Popen(["python3","-"], stdin=subprocess.PIPE, start_new_session=True) snippet. Python-spawns-Python with a sole '-' argument is rare outside of test rigs and uniquely matches the stage-1 RAT loader. Cross-checked against: • https://www.aikido.dev/blog/malicious-pypi-packages-spellcheckpy-and-spellcheckerpy-deliver-python-rat
ATT&CKT1059.006 T1105
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
DeviceProcessEvents

| where InitiatingProcessFileName has "python"
| where FileName has "python"
| where ProcessCommandLine endswith " -" or ProcessCommandLine endswith "python3 -" or ProcessCommandLine endswith "python -" or ProcessCommandLine endswith "python.exe -" or ProcessCommandLine endswith "python3.exe -"
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, FolderPath, InitiatingProcessFolderPath
| order by Timestamp desc
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where NewProcessName has "python"
| where ParentProcessName has "python"
| where CommandLine endswith " -" or CommandLine endswith "python3 -" or CommandLine endswith "python -" or CommandLine endswith "python.exe -" or CommandLine endswith "python3.exe -"
| where TargetUserName !endswith "$"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, NewProcessName, CommandLine, ParentProcessName, ProcessId
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: Python interpreter spawns detached child Python reading from stdin
id: 4d2f8b1c-7e9a-4a3b-9c8d-2f1e5b9c0d44
status: experimental
description: Stage-1 fileless loader pattern from spellcheckpy/spellcheckerpy where a Python process spawns another Python invoked only with '-' to read its script from stdin (subprocess.Popen with start_new_session=True). Enables fileless execution of a fetched RAT payload.
references:
  - https://www.aikido.dev/blog/malicious-pypi-packages-spellcheckpy-and-spellcheckerpy-deliver-python-rat
author: SOC Detection Eng

#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2
| ParentBaseFileName=/^python(3)?(\.exe)?$/i

[LLM] C2 beacon or stage-2 fetch to updatenet[.]work / 172.86.73.139 / dothebest[.]store Command & Control High
Detects outbound HTTP(S) or DNS traffic to the spellcheckpy C2 domain updatenet.work, the RouterHosting/Cloudzy A-record 172.86.73.139, or the prior-campaign C2 dothebest.store (HelixGuard report). The RAT beacons /update1.php every 5 seconds — a single hit on this triplet is high-fidelity. Rationale: Three IOCs named directly by the article: updatenet.work (live C2 + /update1.php beacon + /settings/history.php stage-2), 172.86.73.139 (RouterHosting/Cloudzy A-record), and dothebest.store (prior-campaign C2 from HelixGuard write-up that the article links the same actor to). Each is unique enough that a single hit is investigatable; ContextImageFileName == python.exe with site-packages/spellchecker* in path is the confirmation pivot. Cross-checked against: • https://www.aikido.dev/blog/malicious-pypi-packages-spellcheckpy-and-spellcheckerpy-deliver-python-rat • https://www.helixguard.io/research • https://www.halcyon.ai/research/cloudzy-with-a-chance-of-ransomware
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1573 T1008
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic Network_Resolution.DNS
let c2_domains = dynamic(["updatenet.work","dothebest.store"]);
let c2_ip = "172.86.73.139";
let c2_paths = dynamic(["update1.php","settings/history.php"]);
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where RemoteIP == c2_ip
   or RemoteUrl has_any (c2_domains)
   or RemoteUrl has_any (c2_paths)
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemoteUrl, RemotePort, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFolderPath, InitiatingProcessAccountName
| order by Timestamp desc
let c2_domains = dynamic(["updatenet.work","dothebest.store"]);
let c2_ip = "172.86.73.139";
union isfuzzy=true
  (DnsEvents
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
    | where Name has_any (c2_domains)
    | project TimeGenerated, Host=Computer, ClientIP, Indicator=Name, SourceTable="DnsEvents"),
  (CommonSecurityLog
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
    | where DestinationHostName has_any (c2_domains)
        or DestinationIP == c2_ip
        or RequestURL contains "updatenet.work"
        or RequestURL contains "dothebest.store"
        or RequestURL contains "update1.php"
        or RequestURL contains "settings/history.php"
    | project TimeGenerated, Host=SourceHostName, ClientIP=SourceIP, Indicator=coalesce(DestinationHostName, RequestURL, DestinationIP), SourceTable="CommonSecurityLog"),
  (ImNetworkSession
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
    | where DstHostname has_any (c2_domains)
        or DstIpAddr == c2_ip
        or Url contains "update1.php"
        or Url contains "settings/history.php"
    | project TimeGenerated, Host=DvcHostname, ClientIP=SrcIpAddr, Indicator=coalesce(DstHostname, DstIpAddr, Url), SourceTable="ImNetworkSession")
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: DNS or HTTP traffic to spellcheckpy RAT C2 (updatenet.work / 172.86.73.139 / dothebest.store)
id: 7b1e8a2c-9d4f-4e2a-b3a1-6c8e9f1a2b73
status: experimental
description: Detects DNS resolution or HTTP(S) traffic to the C2 infrastructure used by the spellcheckpy / spellcheckerpy PyPI campaign and the prior dothebest.store campaign documented by HelixGuard. RAT beacons /update1.php every 5 seconds with a custom XOR-encrypted binary protocol.
references:
  - https://www.aikido.dev/blog/malicious-pypi-packages-spellcheckpy-and-spellcheckerpy-deliver-python-rat
author: SOC Detection Eng
date: 2026/05/21
tags:
  - attack.command_and_control
  - attack.t1071.001
  - attack.t1573
logsource:
  category: dns
detection:
  selection:
    QueryName:
      - 'updatenet.work'
      - 'dothebest.store'
      - '*.updatenet.work'
      - '*.dothebest.store'
  condition: selection
falsepositives:
  - Threat-intel sandbox detonating the same package
  - VirusTotal / urlscan crawler enriching the IOC from a security-team egress
  - Security researcher manually browsing the domains
level: high
(@network.destination.ip:172.86.73.139 OR CIDR(@network.destination.ip, 172.86.73.0/24) OR @dns.question.name:(updatenet.work OR *.updatenet.work OR dothebest.store OR *.dothebest.store) OR @url.full:(*updatenet.work* OR *dothebest.store* OR *update1.php* OR *"settings/history.php"*) OR @http.url:(*updatenet.work* OR *dothebest.store* OR *update1.php*))
(#event_simpleName=DnsRequest DomainName=/(updatenet\.work|dothebest\.store)$/i) OR (#event_simpleName=NetworkConnectIP4 RemoteAddressIP4="172.86.73.139")
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, ContextImageFileName, DomainName, RemoteAddressIP4], function=count())
NETWORK
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(All_Traffic.dest_ip) as dest_ip values(All_Traffic.dest_port) as dest_port values(All_Traffic.url) as url from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic where (All_Traffic.dest IN ("updatenet.work","dothebest.store") OR All_Traffic.dest_ip="172.86.73.139" OR All_Traffic.url="*updatenet.work*" OR All_Traffic.url="*dothebest.store*" OR All_Traffic.url="*update1.php*" OR All_Traffic.url="*settings/history.php*") by All_Traffic.src All_Traffic.user All_Traffic.app All_Traffic.dest | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)` | convert ctime(firstTime) ctime(lastTime)
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(All_Traffic.dest_ip) as dest_ip values(All_Traffic.dest_port) as dest_port values(All_Traffic.url) as url from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic where (All_Traffic.dest IN ("updatenet.work","dothebest.store") OR All_Traffic.dest_ip="172.86.73.139" OR All_Traffic.url="*updatenet.work*" OR All_Traffic.url="*dothebest.store*" OR All_Traffic.url="*update1.php*" OR All_Traffic.url="*settings/history.php*") by All_Traffic.src All_Traffic.user All_Traffic.app All_Traffic.dest | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)` | convert ctime(firstTime) ctime(lastTime)
Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations Command & Control Medium
C2 channel detection via inter-beacon-time stddev / fan-out to single dest.
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1071.004
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic DeviceNetworkEvents
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where RemoteIPType == "Public" and ActionType == "ConnectionSuccess"
| project DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort, Timestamp
| sort by DeviceName asc, RemoteIP asc, RemotePort asc, Timestamp asc
| extend prev_dev = prev(DeviceName, 1), prev_ip = prev(RemoteIP, 1),
         prev_port = prev(RemotePort, 1), prev_ts = prev(Timestamp, 1)
| where DeviceName == prev_dev and RemoteIP == prev_ip and RemotePort == prev_port
| extend delta_sec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, prev_ts)
| summarize conn_count = count(), avg_delta = avg(delta_sec), stdev_delta = stdev(delta_sec)
    by DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort
| where conn_count > 30 and avg_delta between (30.0 .. 600.0) and stdev_delta < 5.0
| order by conn_count desc
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(2h)
| where DvcAction != "Block"
| where ipv4_is_private(DstIpAddr) == false
| summarize ConnCount = count(),
            DistinctMinutes = dcount(bin(TimeGenerated, 1m))
            by DvcHostname, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber
| where ConnCount > 50 and DistinctMinutes > 30   // sustained, not bursty
| order by ConnCount desc
NETWORK
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count, values(All_Traffic.dest_port) AS ports
    from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
    where All_Traffic.action="allowed" AND All_Traffic.dest_category!="internal"
    by _time span=10s, All_Traffic.src, All_Traffic.dest
| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`
| streamstats current=f last(_time) AS prev_time by src, dest
| eval delta = _time - prev_time
| stats avg(delta) AS avg_delta stdev(delta) AS sd_delta count by src, dest
| where count > 30 AND sd_delta < 5 AND avg_delta>=30 AND avg_delta<=600
| sort - count
| tstats summariesonly=false count, values(All_Traffic.dest_port) AS ports
    from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
    where All_Traffic.action="allowed" AND All_Traffic.dest_category!="internal"
    by _time span=10s, All_Traffic.src, All_Traffic.dest
| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`
| streamstats current=f last(_time) AS prev_time by src, dest
| eval delta = _time - prev_time
| stats avg(delta) AS avg_delta stdev(delta) AS sd_delta count by src, dest
| where count > 30 AND sd_delta < 5 AND avg_delta>=30 AND avg_delta<=600
| sort - count
Network connections to article IPs / domains Command & Control High
Outbound traffic to attacker infrastructure named in the article.
ATT&CKT1071
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic Web Network_Resolution.DNS DeviceNetworkEvents
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where RemoteIP in ("172.86.73.139") or RemoteUrl has_any ("updatenet.work", "dothebest.store")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, RemoteIP, RemotePort, RemoteUrl,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine
let BadIPs     = dynamic(["172.86.73.139"]);
let BadDomains = dynamic(["updatenet.work", "dothebest.store"]);
ImNetworkSession

title: Crypto-Wallet Keystore Access by Non-Wallet Process
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d02
status: experimental
description: |
    Stealers / wallet drainers read keystore files from MetaMask,
    Exodus, Atomic, Phantom, Bitcoin, Electrum, Ethereum-cli wallets.
    Filtering out the legitimate wallet binaries leaves only attacker
    activity.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1005/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1005
    - attack.collection
logsource:
    category: file_access
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_path:
        TargetFilename|contains:
            - '\Ethereum\keystore\'
            - '\Bitcoin\'
            - '\Exodus\'
            - '\Electrum\wallets\'
            - '\MetaMask\'
            - '\Phantom\'
            - '\Atomic\Local Storage\'
    filter_legit:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\MetaMask.exe'
            - '\Exodus.exe'
            - '\Atomic.exe'
            - '\electrum.exe'
            - '\Bitcoin.exe'
            - '\Phantom.exe'
    condition: selection_path and not filter_legit
falsepositives:
    - Backup software
level: high
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where (Filesystem.file_path="*\Ethereum\keystore\*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Bitcoin\wallet.dat"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Exodus\exodus.wallet*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Electrum\wallets\*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\MetaMask\*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Phantom\*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Atomic\Local Storage\*")
      AND NOT Filesystem.process_name IN ("MetaMask.exe","Exodus.exe","Atomic.exe","electrum.exe","Bitcoin.exe","Phantom.exe")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.process_name, Filesystem.file_path, Filesystem.user
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where (Filesystem.file_path="*\Ethereum\keystore\*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Bitcoin\wallet.dat"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Exodus\exodus.wallet*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Electrum\wallets\*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\MetaMask\*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Phantom\*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Atomic\Local Storage\*")
      AND NOT Filesystem.process_name IN ("MetaMask.exe","Exodus.exe","Atomic.exe","electrum.exe","Bitcoin.exe","Phantom.exe")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.process_name, Filesystem.file_path, Filesystem.user
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`

title: Infostealer - Non-Browser Process Accessing Browser Credential Stores
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d01
status: experimental
description: |
    Stealers (RedLine, Lumma, Vidar, Atomic) read Login Data / cookies
    SQLite databases from Chrome/Edge/Firefox profile directories. Any
    non-browser process touching these files is a high-fidelity signal.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1539/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1555/003/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1539
    - attack.t1555.003
    - attack.credential-access
logsource:
    category: file_access
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_path:
        TargetFilename|contains:
            - '\Google\Chrome\User Data\'
            - '\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\'
            - '\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\'
    selection_file:
        TargetFilename|endswith:
            - '\Login Data'
            - '\Cookies'
            - '\logins.json'
            - '\cookies.sqlite'
    filter_browser:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\chrome.exe'
            - '\msedge.exe'
            - '\firefox.exe'
            - '\brave.exe'
            - '\opera.exe'
    condition: selection_path and selection_file and not filter_browser
falsepositives:
    - Backup utilities reading user profile files
    - Browser sync agents from non-stock vendors
level: high
ENDPOINT

    where (Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Cookies*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\logins.json*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\cookies.sqlite*")
      AND NOT Filesystem.process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.process_name, Filesystem.file_path, Filesystem.user
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where (Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Cookies*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\logins.json*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\cookies.sqlite*")
      AND NOT Filesystem.process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.process_name, Filesystem.file_path, Filesystem.user
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
PowerShell encoded / obfuscated command Exploitation High
Encoded or obfuscated PowerShell — common across loaders, recon, and post-exploitation.
ATT&CKT1059.001 T1027
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceProcessEvents
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe")
| where ProcessCommandLine matches regex @"(?i)(-enc|encodedcommand|frombase64string|-nop|-w\s+hidden|invoke-expression|iex\s*\(|downloadstring|net\.webclient)"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, ProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine
SecurityEvent
