Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad). → Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution
Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code. → Fake CAPTCHA / clipboard-injected PowerShell (ClickFix / FakeCaptcha) · PowerShell encoded / obfuscated command · Trusted vendor binary / installer launching unusual children · Article-specific behavioural hunt — First Sophisticated Malware Discovered on Maven Central via Typosquatting Attack
Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key. → [LLM] Jackson Maven Typosquat Payload Execution (svchosts.exe / payload.bin / known SHA256) · [LLM] JVM-Dropped .idea.pid Persistence Marker or payload.bin in Temp (Jackson Typosquat) · RMM tool installed by non-IT user — remote-access utility for hands-on-keyboard
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking. → [LLM] Jackson Maven Typosquat C2 Beacon to fasterxml.org / 103.127.243.82 · Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations · Network connections to article IPs / domains
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage. → Crypto-wallet file/keystore access by non-wallet process · Infostealer — non-browser process accessing browser cookie/login DBs · Remote service execution — PsExec / SMB lateral movement · Ransomware-style mass file rename / extension change · LSASS process access / dump (credential theft)
[LLM] Jackson Maven Typosquat C2 Beacon to fasterxml.org / 103.127.243.82 Command & Control High
Detects outbound network activity to the attacker-controlled C2 infrastructure used by the malicious org.fasterxml.jackson.core Maven package — the typosquatted domain fasterxml.org (m.fasterxml.org:51211 config server) and the payload-hosting IP 103.127.243.82:8000. Triggers on any DNS resolution, HTTP request, or TCP connection to these IOCs. Rationale: Uses three hard IOCs directly named in the article and corroborated across CyberSecurityNews, SecurityOnline, GBHackers, and SC World: (1) IP 103.127.243.82 (payload host), (2) fasterxml.org / m.fasterxml.org (typosquat — legitimate Jackson uses fasterxml.com), and (3) the unusual high port 51211 used by the config server when contacted by a JVM. fasterxml.org was registered 2025-12-17 specifically for this campaign — no legitimate use exists. Cross-checked against: • https://www.aikido.dev/blog/maven-central-jackson-typosquatting-malware • https://cybersecuritynews.com/hackers-infiltrated-maven-central/ • https://securityonline.info/prefix-swap-panic-sophisticated-jackson-imposter-infiltrates-maven-central/ • https://gbhackers.com/jackson-json-library/ • https://www.scworld.com/brief/maven-central-subjected-to-typosquatted-jackson-json-library • https://www.esecurityplanet.com/threats/malicious-jackson-lookalike-library-slips-into-maven-central/

title: Maven Jackson Typosquat C2 Communication (fasterxml.org / 103.127.243.82)

status: experimental
description: Detects network connections to the C2 infrastructure used by the malicious org.fasterxml.jackson.core Maven Central package (typosquat of com.fasterxml.jackson.core). The package fetches AES-encrypted payload config from m.fasterxml.org:51211/config.txt and downloads platform-specific binaries from 103.127.243.82:8000.

[LLM] Jackson Maven Typosquat Payload Execution (svchosts.exe / payload.bin / known SHA256) Installation High
Detects execution of the Windows second-stage binary svchosts.exe (deliberate typosquat of the legitimate svchost.exe), the staged payload.bin dropper, or the article's known-malicious SHA256 hashes. svchosts.exe as a process image should not exist on a clean Windows host — high-confidence alerting binary. Rationale: `svchosts.exe` (note the trailing 's' — typosquat of `svchost.exe`) is named explicitly in the article as the Windows payload filename and is not a legitimate Microsoft binary. The two SHA256 hashes are pre-extracted IOCs corroborated by Aikido + eSecurity Planet. The Java→Temp→payload.bin chain captures the dropper behaviour described in Stage 4–6 of the malware flow. Cross-checked against: • https://www.aikido.dev/blog/maven-central-jackson-typosquatting-malware • https://www.esecurityplanet.com/threats/malicious-jackson-lookalike-library-slips-into-maven-central/ • https://cybersecuritynews.com/hackers-infiltrated-maven-central/ • https://gbhackers.com/jackson-json-library/
ATT&CKT1036.005 T1204.002 T1059 T1195.002

  "8bce95ebfb895537fec243e069d7193980361de9d916339906b11a14ffded94f"   // Windows svchosts.exe
]);
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where FileName =~ "svchosts.exe"                                                  // deliberate typosquat of svchost.exe
    or FileName =~ "payload.bin"                                                    // article-named dropper artefact
    or SHA256 in (_badHashes)
    or ( InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("java.exe","javaw.exe","javaws.exe")
         and FolderPath has @"\Temp\"
         and FileName in~ ("svchosts.exe","payload.bin","update") )
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessParentFileName
| order by Timestamp desc
let _badHashes = dynamic([

title: Malicious Maven Jackson Payload Execution (svchosts.exe / payload.bin)

status: experimental
description: Detects execution of the Windows second-stage binary svchosts.exe (typosquat of svchost.exe with extra 's'), the payload.bin dropper, or processes matching the known-malicious SHA256 hashes from the org.fasterxml.jackson.core Maven typosquatting campaign.

[LLM] JVM-Dropped .idea.pid Persistence Marker or payload.bin in Temp (Jackson Typosquat) Installation High
Hunts the file-system artefacts uniquely created by the malicious org.fasterxml.jackson.core Spring auto-config: an .idea.pid marker file (disguised as an IntelliJ artefact) used to suppress re-execution, and payload.bin written into the system temp directory, both authored by a java.exe / javaw.exe parent. The .idea.pid filename in particular is a deliberate, attacker-specific naming choice and has near-zero legitimate-use baseline. Rationale: Two article-specific filename artefacts that have no legitimate analogue: (1) `.idea.pid` is an attacker-chosen masquerade (real IntelliJ uses an `.idea/` directory, not a `.pid` file) used as a re-execution guard per Stage 7; (2) `payload.bin` is the canonical dropped binary name from the deobfuscated source code shown in the article. Parent-process scoping to java.exe/javaw.exe keeps FPs near zero. Cross-checked against SecurityOnline write-up which independently confirms the .idea.pid persistence-marker behaviour. Cross-checked against: • https://www.aikido.dev/blog/maven-central-jackson-typosquatting-malware • https://securityonline.info/prefix-swap-panic-sophisticated-jackson-imposter-infiltrates-maven-central/ • https://undercodetesting.com/maven-central-breached-how-hackers-weaponized-a-fake-jackson-library-in-a-sophisticated-supply-chain-attack-video/ • https://www.scworld.com/brief/maven-central-subjected-to-typosquatted-jackson-json-library
ATT&CKT1547 T1036.008 T1105 T1027
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where ActionType in ("FileCreated","FileModified","FileRenamed")
| where ( FileName =~ ".idea.pid" )                                                  // attacker-specific persistence marker
    or ( FileName =~ "payload.bin"                                                  // article-named dropped binary
         and InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("java.exe","javaw.exe","javaws.exe") )
    or ( FolderPath has @"\Temp\"
         and FileName in~ ("svchosts.exe","update")
         and InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("java.exe","javaw.exe","javaws.exe") )
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFolderPath, InitiatingProcessAccountName
| order by Timestamp desc
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where EventType in ("FileCreated","FileModified","FileRenamed")
| where ( TargetFileName =~ ".idea.pid" )
    or ( TargetFileName =~ "payload.bin" and ActingProcessName has_any ("java.exe","javaw.exe","javaws.exe","java","javaw") )
    or ( TargetFilePath has_any (@"\Temp\", "/tmp/")
         and TargetFileName in~ ("svchosts.exe","update")
         and ActingProcessName has_any ("java.exe","javaw.exe","javaws.exe","java","javaw") )
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, TargetFileName, TargetFilePath, TargetFileSHA256, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, ActorUsername
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic DeviceNetworkEvents
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where RemoteIPType == "Public" and ActionType == "ConnectionSuccess"
| project DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort, Timestamp
| sort by DeviceName asc, RemoteIP asc, RemotePort asc, Timestamp asc
| extend prev_dev = prev(DeviceName, 1), prev_ip = prev(RemoteIP, 1),
         prev_port = prev(RemotePort, 1), prev_ts = prev(Timestamp, 1)
| where DeviceName == prev_dev and RemoteIP == prev_ip and RemotePort == prev_port
| extend delta_sec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, prev_ts)
| summarize conn_count = count(), avg_delta = avg(delta_sec), stdev_delta = stdev(delta_sec)
    by DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort
| where conn_count > 30 and avg_delta between (30.0 .. 600.0) and stdev_delta < 5.0
| order by conn_count desc
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(2h)
| where DvcAction != "Block"
| where ipv4_is_private(DstIpAddr) == false
| summarize ConnCount = count(),
            DistinctMinutes = dcount(bin(TimeGenerated, 1m))
            by DvcHostname, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber
| where ConnCount > 50 and DistinctMinutes > 30   // sustained, not bursty
| order by ConnCount desc

Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution Delivery High
User received an external email containing a URL, clicked it, and within 60 seconds the recipient's endpoint spawned a scripting interpreter or network downloader (PowerShell / cmd / mshta / curl / certutil / bitsadmin). This is the high-fidelity shape — a raw "user clicked an emailed URL" query is too noisy to alert on because every Microsoft 365 tenant generates thousands of legitimate clicks per day. The exec-correlation step suppresses the noise to roughly the rate at which a click actually drives onto-host execution, which is the actionable signal. Pair with UC_PHISH_LINK_BYPASS (Safe Links override) and UC_PHISH_LINK_NEWDOMAIN for orthogonal high-fidelity variants.
ATT&CKT1566.002 T1204.001 T1059.001
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Web Endpoint.Processes EmailEvents EmailUrlInfo UrlClickEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s.
// Far higher fidelity than "every clicked URL" — most legitimate clicks
// never spawn a non-browser child process, so the join eliminates the
// 99% of noise that makes a raw click query unactionable.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectClicks = UrlClickEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | where ActionType in ("ClickAllowed","ClickedThrough")
    | join kind=inner (
        EmailEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
        | where DeliveryAction == "Delivered"
        | where EmailDirection == "Inbound"
        | project NetworkMessageId, Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain,
                  RecipientEmailAddress, EmailTimestamp = Timestamp
      ) on NetworkMessageId
    | join kind=leftouter (
        EmailUrlInfo | project NetworkMessageId, Url, UrlDomain
      ) on NetworkMessageId, Url
    | project ClickTime = Timestamp, AccountUpn, IPAddress, Url, UrlDomain,
              Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain, RecipientEmailAddress,
              ActionType;
// Correlate to a non-browser child process spawned within 60 seconds on
// the recipient's device.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                         "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                        "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                        "bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectClicks on $left.AccountName == $right.AccountUpn
| where Timestamp between (ClickTime .. ClickTime + 60s)
| project ClickTime, ProcessTime = Timestamp,
          DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, ClickTime),
          DeviceName, AccountName, RecipientEmailAddress, SenderFromAddress,
          Subject, Url, UrlDomain, ActionType,
          FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by ClickTime desc
// UrlClickEvents has no clean Sentinel-native equivalent. The detection
// pivots to: Office Send→Receive proximity to SecurityEvent 4688 of a
// non-browser child process. Lower fidelity than the Defender version.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectMailUsers = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation =~ "Receive"
    | summarize Subject = any(Subject), Sender = any(Sender)
                by MailboxOwnerUPN, MessageId, EmailTime = bin(TimeGenerated, 1m);
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("\chrome.exe","\msedge.exe",
                                     "\firefox.exe","\outlook.exe","\brave.exe")
| where NewProcessName has_any ("\powershell.exe","\pwsh.exe","\cmd.exe",
                                  "\mshta.exe","\rundll32.exe","\regsvr32.exe",
                                  "\wscript.exe","\cscript.exe","\bitsadmin.exe",
                                  "\certutil.exe","\curl.exe","\wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectMailUsers on $left.Account == $right.MailboxOwnerUPN
| where TimeGenerated between (EmailTime .. EmailTime + 60s)
| project TimeGenerated, EmailTime, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine, Sender, Subject
| order by TimeGenerated desc
WEB
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,
        clicked_domain, clicked_url, exec_proc, exec_cmd
| sort - click_time

Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceEvents

[LLM] Vulnerable WindowsCodecs.dll (CVE-2025-50165) present on endpoint Exploitation High
Surface hosts running WindowsCodecs.dll versions between 10.0.26100.0 and 10.0.26100.4945 that contain the uninitialized function pointer dereference reachable via 12-bit/16-bit JPG re-encoding. Pivots on the exact vulnerable SHA-1 from ESET's analysis and the Defender TVM CVE catalogue. Rationale: ESET names both the vulnerable build (10.0.26100.4768, SHA-1 5887D96565749067564BABCD3DC5D107AB6666BD) and the patched build (10.0.26100.4946, SHA-1 4EC1DC0431432BC318E78C520387911EC44F84FC). Hash-pinning gives near-zero false positives versus generic CVE banners. Cross-checked with the original Zscaler ThreatLabz disclosure and Microsoft MSRC's CVE entry. Cross-checked against: • https://www.zscaler.com/blogs/security-research/technical-analysis-cve-2025-50165 • https://msrc.microsoft.com/update-guide/vulnerability/CVE-2025-50165
ATT&CKT1203
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem
// Path A: TVM catalogue hit for CVE-2025-50165

| where CveId == "CVE-2025-50165"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, SoftwareVendor, SoftwareName, SoftwareVersion, VulnerabilitySeverityLevel, RecommendedSecurityUpdate
| union (
    // Path B: image-load of the vulnerable WindowsCodecs.dll hash from ESET (10.0.26100.4768)
    DeviceImageLoadEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
    | where FileName =~ "WindowsCodecs.dll"
    | where SHA1 =~ "5887D96565749067564BABCD3DC5D107AB6666BD"
    | summarize FirstSeen=min(Timestamp), LastSeen=max(Timestamp), LoadingProcs=make_set(InitiatingProcessFileName, 25) by DeviceName, FolderPath, SHA1
)
| order by DeviceName asc
DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where CveId == "CVE-2025-50165"
| project TimeGenerated, DeviceName, SoftwareVendor, SoftwareName, SoftwareVersion, VulnerabilitySeverityLevel, RecommendedSecurityUpdate
| order by DeviceName asc

[LLM] Process crash with faulting module WindowsCodecs.dll (CVE-2025-50165 exploit attempt) Exploitation Medium
Hunts for application crashes where the faulting module is WindowsCodecs.dll inside a process that handles JPG re-encoding (Explorer thumbnails, image editors, Office, browsers). The ESET analysis shows the crash signature is dereference of 0xBAADF00D inside jpeg_finish_compress when a 12/16-bit JPG is re-encoded — a process crash with WindowsCodecs.dll on the stack is a high-fidelity exploit-attempt indicator on unpatched hosts. Rationale: ESET demonstrates the crash signature inside WindowsCodecs.dll's jpeg_finish_compress — 0xBAADF00D dereference. Application Error EID 1000 / WerFault invocations naming WindowsCodecs.dll as faulting module in JPG-handling parents (Explorer thumbnail extraction via dllhost.exe, Photos.exe, Office, browsers, Acrobat, Photoshop) are scoped to plausible attack vectors per Microsoft's WIC re-encode code path. The list of JPG-handling parents is from MS WIC documentation linked in the article. Cross-checked against: • https://www.zscaler.com/blogs/security-research/technical-analysis-cve-2025-50165 • https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/wic/-wic-codec-jpegmetadataencoding
ATT&CKT1203 T1059
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(14d)
| where FileName =~ "WerFault.exe"
| where ProcessCommandLine has "WindowsCodecs" or ProcessCommandLine has "windowscodecs.dll"
| extend FaultingHost = InitiatingProcessFileName
| where FaultingHost in~ ("explorer.exe","thumbnailcache.exe","dllhost.exe","photos.exe","mspaint.exe","winword.exe","excel.exe","powerpnt.exe","outlook.exe","chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","acrord32.exe","acrobat.exe","photoshop.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, FaultingHost, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, ProcessCommandLine, AccountName, InitiatingProcessAccountName
| join kind=leftouter (
    DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities | where CveId == "CVE-2025-50165" | project DeviceName, IsVulnerable=true
) on DeviceName

[LLM] NosyDoor AppDomainManager hijack: UevAppMonitor.exe executing from non-standard path Installation High
Hunts the NosyDoor stage-2 LOLBin: the legitimate UevAppMonitor.exe is normally only present in C:\Windows\System32, but LongNosedGoblin's dropper copies it to C:\Windows\Microsoft.NET\Framework so it loads a sibling .config that triggers AppDomainManager injection from SharedReg.dll. Execution of UevAppMonitor.exe from any path other than System32 is highly indicative of NosyDoor stage-2. Rationale: UevAppMonitor.exe is a real Microsoft UE-V binary that ships only in System32; ESET explicitly notes the dropper copies it to C:\Windows\Microsoft.NET\Framework, then loads SharedReg.dll through a crafted .config (AppDomainManager injection). Cross-checked against The Hacker News and SecurityWeek coverage which restate the same path / DLL. Cross-checked against: • https://thehackernews.com/2025/12/china-aligned-threat-group-uses-windows.html • https://www.securityweek.com/chinese-apt-longnosedgoblin-targeting-asian-governments/ • https://www.helpnetsecurity.com/2025/12/18/eset-china-aligned-apt-group-policy/ • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1574/014/
ATT&CKT1574.014 T1218 T1036.005
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes Endpoint.Filesystem
// LongNosedGoblin NosyDoor stage-2 — UevAppMonitor.exe is a legitimate Windows binary that *only* ships in System32. Execution from anywhere else (especially Microsoft.NET\Framework) means a copy was staged by the dropper to side-load SharedReg.dll via AppDomainManager.
let UevExec =
    DeviceProcessEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(30d)
    | where FileName =~ "UevAppMonitor.exe"
    | where not(FolderPath startswith @"C:\Windows\System32\")
    | where not(FolderPath startswith @"C:\Windows\SysWOW64\")
    | project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FolderPath, ProcessCommandLine,
              InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
              InitiatingProcessFolderPath, SHA256;
let SharedRegLoad =
    DeviceImageLoadEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(30d)
    | where InitiatingProcessFileName =~ "UevAppMonitor.exe"
    | where FileName =~ "SharedReg.dll"
    | where not(FolderPath startswith @"C:\Windows\WinSxS\")
    | project Timestamp, DeviceName, FolderPath, FileName, SHA256,
              InitiatingProcessFolderPath;
UevExec
| union SharedRegLoad
| order by Timestamp desc
// LongNosedGoblin NosyDoor stage-2 — legitimate UevAppMonitor.exe staged outside System32
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where NewProcessName endswith @"\UevAppMonitor.exe"
| where not(NewProcessName startswith @"C:\Windows\System32\")
| where not(NewProcessName startswith @"C:\Windows\SysWOW64\")
| where Account !endswith "$"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, NewProcessName, CommandLine,
          ParentProcessName, ProcessId, TokenElevationType
| order by TimeGenerated desc

[LLM] NosyDoor persistence: scheduled task 'OneDrive Reporting Task-S-1-5-21-' under Microsoft folder Installation High
NosyDoor's dropper persists by creating a scheduled task with the literal prefix 'OneDrive Reporting Task-S-1-5-21-' followed by a random GUID, registered under the Microsoft task folder, executing the relocated UevAppMonitor.exe at startup. The naming pattern is article-unique and not used by Microsoft OneDrive itself. Rationale: ESET reports the dropper creates a Windows scheduled task literally named 'OneDrive Reporting Task-S-1-5-21-<GUID>' under the Microsoft task folder to autorun the relocated UevAppMonitor.exe at startup. The literal prefix plus the SID-style suffix is article-unique — legitimate OneDrive tasks do not embed an S-1-5-21 SID in their name. Cross-checked against: • https://thehackernews.com/2025/12/china-aligned-threat-group-uses-windows.html • https://cyberpress.org/apt-hackers-china-malware/ • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1053/005/
ATT&CKT1053.005 T1036.005

| where FolderPath has @"\Windows\System32\Tasks\Microsoft\"
| where FileName startswith "OneDrive Reporting Task-S-1-5-21-"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, FolderPath, FileName,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessFolderPath,
          InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessAccountName,
          InitiatingProcessAccountSid, SHA256
| order by Timestamp desc
// LongNosedGoblin NosyDoor — TaskScheduler 4698 with NosyDoor task-name prefix
SecurityEvent

| extend XmlData = parse_xml(EventData)
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, SubjectUserName, SubjectDomainName,
          SubjectLogonId, EventData
| order by TimeGenerated desc

[LLM] NosyDoor dropper file artefacts in C:\Windows\Microsoft.NET\Framework Installation High
Hunts the four-file drop the NosyDoor stage-1 dropper writes into C:\Windows\Microsoft.NET\Framework — SharedReg.dll, log.cached, netfxsbs9.hkf and UevAppMonitor.exe.config — names deliberately chosen to blend with legitimate SharedReg12.dll / netfxsbs12.hkf. None of these filenames are produced by genuine .NET Framework installation/servicing, so any user-mode write into that directory is a strong NosyDoor staging signal. Rationale: ESET names the exact four files the dropper writes to C:\Windows\Microsoft.NET\Framework (SharedReg.dll, log.cached, netfxsbs9.hkf, UevAppMonitor.exe.config) and explicitly notes their goal is to blend with the genuine SharedReg12.dll / netfxsbs12.hkf — so the '9' vs '12' suffix and the unsuffixed SharedReg.dll are themselves diagnostic. The 'co-occurrence ≥ 2 of N' threshold (skipping Sigma because that's a count predicate) keeps FP rate low while catching variants where one filename rotates. Cross-checked against: • https://thehackernews.com/2025/12/china-aligned-threat-group-uses-windows.html • https://www.securityweek.com/chinese-apt-longnosedgoblin-targeting-asian-governments/ • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1574/014/
ATT&CKT1036.005 T1574.014
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem
// LongNosedGoblin NosyDoor dropper — writes a known set of artefacts into C:\Windows\Microsoft.NET\Framework so the relocated UevAppMonitor.exe loads SharedReg.dll via .config-driven AppDomainManager injection.
let NosyDoorFiles = dynamic([
    "SharedReg.dll",
    "log.cached",
    "netfxsbs9.hkf",            // typo of legitimate netfxsbs12.hkf
    "UevAppMonitor.exe.config",
    "UevAppMonitor.exe",         // staged copy from System32
    "error.txt"                  // dropped on stage-2 decryption errors
]);
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where ActionType in ("FileCreated", "FileModified", "FileRenamed")
| where FolderPath in~ (@"C:\Windows\Microsoft.NET\Framework", @"C:\Windows\Microsoft.NET\Framework64")
   or FolderPath endswith @"\Microsoft.NET\Framework"
   or FolderPath endswith @"\Microsoft.NET\Framework64"
| where FileName in~ (NosyDoorFiles)
// Exclude legitimate .NET servicing — the genuine SharedReg DLL is named SharedReg12.dll, not SharedReg.dll
| where not(InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("TrustedInstaller.exe", "msiexec.exe", "setup.exe") and InitiatingProcessFolderPath startswith @"C:\Windows\")
| summarize FileSet = make_set(FileName), FirstSeen = min(Timestamp), LastSeen = max(Timestamp),
            Writers = make_set(InitiatingProcessFileName)
  by DeviceName, FolderPath, InitiatingProcessAccountName
| where array_length(FileSet) >= 2     // at least two of the four sibling artefacts
| order by LastSeen desc
// Sentinel equivalent via ASIM ImFileEvent — NosyDoor dropper artefact set
let NosyDoorFiles = dynamic(["SharedReg.dll","log.cached","netfxsbs9.hkf","UevAppMonitor.exe.config","UevAppMonitor.exe","error.txt"]);
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where EventType in ("FileCreated","FileModified","FileRenamed")
| where TargetFilePath has @"\Windows\Microsoft.NET\Framework"
| where TargetFileName in~ (NosyDoorFiles)
| where not(ActingProcessName has_any ("TrustedInstaller.exe","msiexec.exe"))
| summarize FileSet = make_set(TargetFileName), FirstSeen = min(TimeGenerated), LastSeen = max(TimeGenerated),
            Writers = make_set(ActingProcessName)
          by DvcHostname, ActorUsername
| where array_length(FileSet) >= 2
| order by LastSeen desc
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(Filesystem.file_name) as files_seen FROM datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem WHERE (Filesystem.file_path="*\\Windows\\Microsoft.NET\\Framework\\*" OR Filesystem.file_path="*\\Windows\\Microsoft.NET\\Framework64\\*") AND (Filesystem.file_name="SharedReg.dll" OR Filesystem.file_name="log.cached" OR Filesystem.file_name="netfxsbs9.hkf" OR Filesystem.file_name="UevAppMonitor.exe.config" OR Filesystem.file_name="UevAppMonitor.exe" OR Filesystem.file_name="error.txt") BY Filesystem.dest Filesystem.user Filesystem.process_name Filesystem.process_path | `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)` | where mvcount(files_seen) >= 2 | `security_content_ctime(firstTime)` | `security_content_ctime(lastTime)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(Filesystem.file_name) as files_seen FROM datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem WHERE (Filesystem.file_path="*\\Windows\\Microsoft.NET\\Framework\\*" OR Filesystem.file_path="*\\Windows\\Microsoft.NET\\Framework64\\*") AND (Filesystem.file_name="SharedReg.dll" OR Filesystem.file_name="log.cached" OR Filesystem.file_name="netfxsbs9.hkf" OR Filesystem.file_name="UevAppMonitor.exe.config" OR Filesystem.file_name="UevAppMonitor.exe" OR Filesystem.file_name="error.txt") BY Filesystem.dest Filesystem.user Filesystem.process_name Filesystem.process_path | `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)` | where mvcount(files_seen) >= 2 | `security_content_ctime(firstTime)` | `security_content_ctime(lastTime)`
Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations Command & Control Medium
C2 channel detection via inter-beacon-time stddev / fan-out to single dest.
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1071.004
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic DeviceNetworkEvents
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where RemoteIPType == "Public" and ActionType == "ConnectionSuccess"
| project DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort, Timestamp
| sort by DeviceName asc, RemoteIP asc, RemotePort asc, Timestamp asc
| extend prev_dev = prev(DeviceName, 1), prev_ip = prev(RemoteIP, 1),
         prev_port = prev(RemotePort, 1), prev_ts = prev(Timestamp, 1)
| where DeviceName == prev_dev and RemoteIP == prev_ip and RemotePort == prev_port
| extend delta_sec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, prev_ts)
| summarize conn_count = count(), avg_delta = avg(delta_sec), stdev_delta = stdev(delta_sec)
    by DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort
| where conn_count > 30 and avg_delta between (30.0 .. 600.0) and stdev_delta < 5.0
| order by conn_count desc
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(2h)
| where DvcAction != "Block"
| where ipv4_is_private(DstIpAddr) == false
| summarize ConnCount = count(),
            DistinctMinutes = dcount(bin(TimeGenerated, 1m))
            by DvcHostname, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber
| where ConnCount > 50 and DistinctMinutes > 30   // sustained, not bursty
| order by ConnCount desc
NETWORK
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count, values(All_Traffic.dest_port) AS ports
    from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
    where All_Traffic.action="allowed" AND All_Traffic.dest_category!="internal"
    by _time span=10s, All_Traffic.src, All_Traffic.dest
| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`
| streamstats current=f last(_time) AS prev_time by src, dest
| eval delta = _time - prev_time
| stats avg(delta) AS avg_delta stdev(delta) AS sd_delta count by src, dest
| where count > 30 AND sd_delta < 5 AND avg_delta>=30 AND avg_delta<=600
| sort - count
| tstats summariesonly=false count, values(All_Traffic.dest_port) AS ports
    from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
    where All_Traffic.action="allowed" AND All_Traffic.dest_category!="internal"
    by _time span=10s, All_Traffic.src, All_Traffic.dest
| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`
| streamstats current=f last(_time) AS prev_time by src, dest
| eval delta = _time - prev_time
| stats avg(delta) AS avg_delta stdev(delta) AS sd_delta count by src, dest
| where count > 30 AND sd_delta < 5 AND avg_delta>=30 AND avg_delta<=600
| sort - count

title: PsExec / SMB Lateral Movement Tooling Execution

Actions on Objectives
Detected
Reconnaissance. Attacker researches the target — OSINT, scanning, enumeration.
Weaponization. Coupling exploit code with deliverable payload (e.g. weaponized PDF/Office doc, trojanized installer).
Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad). → Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution · Email attachment opened from external sender
Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code. → Office app spawning script/LOLBin child process · Fake CAPTCHA / clipboard-injected PowerShell (ClickFix / FakeCaptcha)
Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key.
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking.
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage. → Infostealer — non-browser process accessing browser cookie/login DBs · Ransomware-style mass file rename / extension change · LSASS process access / dump (credential theft) · Remote service execution — PsExec / SMB lateral movement
Infostealer — non-browser process accessing browser cookie/login DBs Actions on Objectives High
Stealers (RedLine, Lumma, Vidar, Atomic) read Login Data / cookies SQLite from Chrome/Edge/Firefox.
ATT&CKT1539 T1555.003
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem DeviceFileEvents
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
| where FolderPath has_any (@"\Google\Chrome\User Data\", @"\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\", @"\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\")
| where FileName in~ ("Login Data","Cookies","logins.json","cookies.sqlite")
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, FolderPath, FileName, ActionType

// ASIM ImFileEvent — covers MDE, Sysmon, AuditD, Defender for Cloud, etc.
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
| where TargetFilePath has_any (@"\Google\Chrome\User Data\",
                                  @"\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\",
                                  @"\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\")
| where TargetFileName in~ ("Login Data","Cookies","logins.json","cookies.sqlite")
| where ActingProcessName !in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName,
          TargetFilePath, TargetFileName, EventType

title: Infostealer - Non-Browser Process Accessing Browser Credential Stores
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d01
status: experimental
description: |
    Stealers (RedLine, Lumma, Vidar, Atomic) read Login Data / cookies
    SQLite databases from Chrome/Edge/Firefox profile directories. Any
    non-browser process touching these files is a high-fidelity signal.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1539/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1555/003/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1539
    - attack.t1555.003
    - attack.credential-access
logsource:
    category: file_access
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_path:
        TargetFilename|contains:
            - '\Google\Chrome\User Data\'
            - '\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\'
            - '\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\'
    selection_file:
        TargetFilename|endswith:
            - '\Login Data'
            - '\Cookies'
            - '\logins.json'
            - '\cookies.sqlite'
    filter_browser:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\chrome.exe'
            - '\msedge.exe'
            - '\firefox.exe'
            - '\brave.exe'
            - '\opera.exe'
    condition: selection_path and selection_file and not filter_browser
falsepositives:
    - Backup utilities reading user profile files
    - Browser sync agents from non-stock vendors
level: high
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where (Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Cookies*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\logins.json*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\cookies.sqlite*")
      AND NOT Filesystem.process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.process_name, Filesystem.file_path, Filesystem.user
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where (Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Cookies*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\logins.json*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\cookies.sqlite*")
      AND NOT Filesystem.process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.process_name, Filesystem.file_path, Filesystem.user
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution Delivery High
User received an external email containing a URL, clicked it, and within 60 seconds the recipient's endpoint spawned a scripting interpreter or network downloader (PowerShell / cmd / mshta / curl / certutil / bitsadmin). This is the high-fidelity shape — a raw "user clicked an emailed URL" query is too noisy to alert on because every Microsoft 365 tenant generates thousands of legitimate clicks per day. The exec-correlation step suppresses the noise to roughly the rate at which a click actually drives onto-host execution, which is the actionable signal. Pair with UC_PHISH_LINK_BYPASS (Safe Links override) and UC_PHISH_LINK_NEWDOMAIN for orthogonal high-fidelity variants.
ATT&CKT1566.002 T1204.001 T1059.001
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Web Endpoint.Processes EmailEvents EmailUrlInfo UrlClickEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s.
// Far higher fidelity than "every clicked URL" — most legitimate clicks
// never spawn a non-browser child process, so the join eliminates the
// 99% of noise that makes a raw click query unactionable.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectClicks = UrlClickEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | where ActionType in ("ClickAllowed","ClickedThrough")
    | join kind=inner (
        EmailEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
        | where DeliveryAction == "Delivered"
        | where EmailDirection == "Inbound"
        | project NetworkMessageId, Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain,
                  RecipientEmailAddress, EmailTimestamp = Timestamp
      ) on NetworkMessageId
    | join kind=leftouter (
        EmailUrlInfo | project NetworkMessageId, Url, UrlDomain
      ) on NetworkMessageId, Url
    | project ClickTime = Timestamp, AccountUpn, IPAddress, Url, UrlDomain,
              Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain, RecipientEmailAddress,
              ActionType;
// Correlate to a non-browser child process spawned within 60 seconds on
// the recipient's device.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                         "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                        "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                        "bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectClicks on $left.AccountName == $right.AccountUpn
| where Timestamp between (ClickTime .. ClickTime + 60s)
| project ClickTime, ProcessTime = Timestamp,
          DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, ClickTime),
          DeviceName, AccountName, RecipientEmailAddress, SenderFromAddress,
          Subject, Url, UrlDomain, ActionType,
          FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by ClickTime desc
// UrlClickEvents has no clean Sentinel-native equivalent. The detection
// pivots to: Office Send→Receive proximity to SecurityEvent 4688 of a
// non-browser child process. Lower fidelity than the Defender version.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectMailUsers = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation =~ "Receive"
    | summarize Subject = any(Subject), Sender = any(Sender)
                by MailboxOwnerUPN, MessageId, EmailTime = bin(TimeGenerated, 1m);
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("\chrome.exe","\msedge.exe",
                                     "\firefox.exe","\outlook.exe","\brave.exe")
| where NewProcessName has_any ("\powershell.exe","\pwsh.exe","\cmd.exe",
                                  "\mshta.exe","\rundll32.exe","\regsvr32.exe",
                                  "\wscript.exe","\cscript.exe","\bitsadmin.exe",
                                  "\certutil.exe","\curl.exe","\wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectMailUsers on $left.Account == $right.MailboxOwnerUPN
| where TimeGenerated between (EmailTime .. EmailTime + 60s)
| project TimeGenerated, EmailTime, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine, Sender, Subject
| order by TimeGenerated desc

``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,
        clicked_domain, clicked_url, exec_proc, exec_cmd
| sort - click_time

Email attachment opened from external sender Delivery High
Attachment delivery + execution by recipient — most common malware initial access.
ATT&CKT1566.001 T1204.002
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Endpoint.Processes EmailAttachmentInfo DeviceProcessEvents
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let MalAttachments = EmailAttachmentInfo
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | project NetworkMessageId, RecipientEmailAddress,
              AttachmentFileName = FileName, AttachmentSHA256 = SHA256;
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("OUTLOOK.EXE","winword.exe","excel.exe","powerpnt.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                      "mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe")
| join kind=inner MalAttachments on $left.AccountUpn == $right.RecipientEmailAddress
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, AttachmentFileName, AttachmentSHA256
// Sentinel doesn't have an attachment-hash table. Best approximation:
// OfficeActivity Send/Receive activity + correlate to host process spawn.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let MailWithAttach = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation in~ ("Send","Receive")
    | where isnotempty(MessageId)
    | project EmailTime = TimeGenerated, MailboxOwnerUPN, Sender,
              Recipients, Subject, MessageId;
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName endswith "OUTLOOK.EXE"
| where NewProcessName endswith "\cmd.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\powershell.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\wscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\cscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\mshta.exe"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, NewProcessName, CommandLine,
          ParentProcessName
| order by TimeGenerated desc

title: Office Application Spawning Script Host

title: FakeCaptcha / ClickFix - Clipboard-Injected PowerShell from Explorer
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d06
status: experimental
description: |
    "FakeCaptcha" / "ClickFix" social-engineering: malicious site asks
    user to press Win+R and paste a payload. The result is
    powershell/mshta launched directly from explorer.exe with iex /
    base64 / downloadstring in the command line.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1059/001/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1204/002/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1059.001
    - attack.t1204.002
    - attack.execution
logsource:
    category: process_creation
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_parent:
        ParentImage|endswith:
            - '\explorer.exe'
            - '\RuntimeBroker.exe'
    selection_child:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\powershell.exe'
            - '\pwsh.exe'
            - '\mshta.exe'
    selection_cmd:
        CommandLine|contains:
            - 'iex'
            - 'invoke-expression'
            - 'frombase64'
            - 'downloadstring'
            - 'hxxp'
            - 'curl '
            - 'wget '
    condition: selection_parent and selection_child and selection_cmd
falsepositives:
    - IT-driven scripted automation that admins paste-launch
level: high
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("explorer.exe","RuntimeBroker.exe")
      AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","mshta.exe")
      AND (Processes.process="*iex*" OR Processes.process="*Invoke-Expression*"
        OR Processes.process="*FromBase64*" OR Processes.process="*DownloadString*"
        OR Processes.process="*hxxp*" OR Processes.process="*curl*" OR Processes.process="*wget*")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.process, Processes.parent_process_name
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("explorer.exe","RuntimeBroker.exe")
      AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","mshta.exe")
      AND (Processes.process="*iex*" OR Processes.process="*Invoke-Expression*"
        OR Processes.process="*FromBase64*" OR Processes.process="*DownloadString*"
        OR Processes.process="*hxxp*" OR Processes.process="*curl*" OR Processes.process="*wget*")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.process, Processes.parent_process_name
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
Ransomware-style mass file rename / extension change Actions on Objectives Medium
Threshold detection: many files renamed in short window, often with new extension.
ATT&CKT1486
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem DeviceFileEvents
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
| where ActionType in ("FileRenamed","FileModified")
| summarize files = dcount(FileName) by DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, bin(Timestamp, 1m)
| where files > 200    // empirical: > 200 unique-file renames in 1m by one account on one host
                       //            is well above the P99 of legitimate bulk-tooling
| order by files desc

ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)
| where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
| where EventType in ("FileRenamed","FileModified")
| summarize files = dcount(TargetFileName)
            by DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, bin(TimeGenerated, 1m)
| where files > 200    // P99 of legit bulk-tooling per-minute rename volume
| order by files desc
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count, dc(Filesystem.file_name) AS files
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where Filesystem.action IN ("modified","renamed")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.user, _time span=1m
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
| where files > 200
| sort - files
| tstats summariesonly=false count, dc(Filesystem.file_name) AS files
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where Filesystem.action IN ("modified","renamed")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.user, _time span=1m
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
| where files > 200
| sort - files
LSASS process access / dump (credential theft) Actions on Objectives High
Mimikatz, comsvcs.dll MiniDump, or any non-Windows process opening LSASS.
ATT&CKT1003.001 T1003
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceEvents
DeviceEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where ActionType == "OpenProcessApiCall"
| where FileName =~ "lsass.exe"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("MsSense.exe","MsMpEng.exe","csrss.exe",
                                          "svchost.exe","wininit.exe","services.exe",
                                          "lsm.exe","SearchProtocolHost.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFolderPath, AccountName
| order by Timestamp desc
// SecurityEvent EventID 4663 = object access. AccessMask 0x10 / 0x40 / 0x1010
// indicate read access to lsass.exe — credential-dump signature. Audit
// Object Access > Audit File System policy required.
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4663
| where ObjectName endswith "\lsass.exe"
| where Account !endswith "$"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, ObjectName, ProcessName,
          AccessMask, AccessReason
| order by TimeGenerated desc

            - '\csrss.exe'
            - '\svchost.exe'

    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.process_name, Processes.process, Processes.parent_process_name
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where (Processes.process="*lsass*" OR Processes.process="*sekurlsa*"

        OR Processes.process="*procdump*lsass*")
       OR (Processes.process_name="rundll32.exe" AND Processes.process="*comsvcs*MiniDump*")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.process_name, Processes.process, Processes.parent_process_name

id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d03
status: experimental
description: |

    pivots over SMB. Pair with `wmic /node:` for the full cluster.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1021/002/

author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02

    - attack.execution

    category: process_creation
    product: windows

            - '\psexec.exe'
            - '\psexec64.exe'
            - '\psexesvc.exe'
            - '\paexec.exe'
            - '\csexec.exe'

level: high

| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.process_name IN ("psexec.exe","psexesvc.exe","paexec.exe","smbexec.py")

id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d09
status: experimental

    A signed vendor binary (in the article's named-vendors list)
    spawning script-host or LOLBin children. Strongest signal when
    paired with a recent CVE / supply-chain advisory naming the same
    vendor.

title: Trusted Vendor Binary Launching Unusual Children
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d09
status: experimental
description: |
    A signed vendor binary (in the article's named-vendors list)
    spawning script-host or LOLBin children. Strongest signal when
    paired with a recent CVE / supply-chain advisory naming the same
    vendor.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1195/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:

    - attack.initial-access
logsource:
    category: process_creation
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_child:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\powershell.exe'
            - '\pwsh.exe'
            - '\cmd.exe'
            - '\rundll32.exe'
            - '\regsvr32.exe'
            - '\mshta.exe'
            - '\wscript.exe'
            - '\cscript.exe'
            - '\wmic.exe'
            - '\bitsadmin.exe'
    selection_parent_vendor:
        ParentImage|contains:
            - '\Program Files\'
            - '\Program Files (x86)\'
    condition: selection_child and selection_parent_vendor
falsepositives:

      article before alerting.
level: medium

[LLM] Vulnerable react-server-dom-* package versions (CVE-2025-55182) in workload inventory Reconnaissance High
Identifies hosts running react-server-dom-webpack / react-server-dom-parcel / react-server-dom-turbopack at versions 19.0.0, 19.1.0, 19.1.1, or 19.2.0 — the exact builds Snyk and Meta name as exploitable for unauthenticated RCE via the RSC Flight protocol. Used pre-patch to scope exposure and post-patch to verify completion. Rationale: Anchors on the three exact package names (react-server-dom-webpack/parcel/turbopack) and four exact vulnerable versions Snyk enumerates, plus CveId CVE-2025-55182. Joined with DeviceInfo.IsInternetFacing so internet-exposed Next.js workloads can be prioritised, matching Snyk's stated 39% cloud-exposure figure. Cross-checked against: • https://snyk.io/blog/security-advisory-critical-rce-vulnerabilities-react-server-components/ • https://github.com/facebook/react/security/advisories • https://github.com/vercel/next.js/security/advisories

[LLM] Node.js process spawning interactive shell — suspected post-exploit RCE on Next.js / RSC server Exploitation High
Hunts for node.exe / node spawning cmd.exe, powershell.exe, pwsh.exe, sh, or bash on hosts running Next.js or any framework embedding react-server-dom-*. Production Node web servers virtually never need a child shell; this is the highest-fidelity behavioural signature of CVE-2025-55182 exploitation reaching command execution. Rationale: Snyk states the RCE 'occurs before any routing logic or auth gates' on a single crafted HTTP request to an RSC endpoint, so the post-exploit foothold lives inside the Node.js process serving that endpoint. A node-parented shell is the cleanest article-specific behavioural pivot. Build-time exclusions (`next build`/`next dev`, npm/yarn/pnpm parents) suppress the only realistic FP source. Cross-checked against: • https://snyk.io/blog/security-advisory-critical-rce-vulnerabilities-react-server-components/ • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1190/
ATT&CKT1059.001 T1059.003 T1059.004 T1190

| where FileName in~ ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","sh","bash","dash","zsh","ash")
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where AccountName !in~ ("system","local service","network service")
| where InitiatingProcessCommandLine !has "next build"
      and InitiatingProcessCommandLine !has "next dev"
      and InitiatingProcessParentFileName !in~ ("npm.exe","npm","yarn.exe","yarn","pnpm.exe","pnpm","npm-cli.js")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName,
          ParentImage = InitiatingProcessFolderPath,
          ParentCmd   = InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          GrandparentImage = InitiatingProcessParentFileName,
          ChildImage  = FolderPath,
          ChildCmd    = ProcessCommandLine,
          SHA256
| order by Timestamp desc
ImProcessCreate

| where ParentProcessName matches regex @"(?i)(^|[\\/])node(\.exe)?$"
| where ActingProcessName matches regex @"(?i)(^|[\\/])(cmd\.exe|powershell\.exe|pwsh\.exe|sh|bash|dash|zsh|ash)$"
| where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
| where ParentProcessCommandLine !has "next build" and ParentProcessCommandLine !has "next dev"
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ParentProcessName, ParentProcessCommandLine, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, SHA256
| order by TimeGenerated desc

detection:
  selection_parent:
    ParentImage|endswith:
      - '\node.exe'
      - '/node'
  selection_child:
    Image|endswith:
      - '\cmd.exe'
      - '\powershell.exe'
      - '\pwsh.exe'
      - '/sh'
      - '/bash'
      - '/dash'
      - '/zsh'
      - '/ash'
  filter_build:
    ParentCommandLine|contains:
      - 'next build'
      - 'next dev'
  filter_pkg_manager:
    ParentImage|endswith:
      - '\npm.exe'
      - '\yarn.exe'
      - '\pnpm.exe'
  condition: selection_parent and selection_child and not (filter_build or filter_pkg_manager)
falsepositives:
  - Next.js build pipelines invoking shell helpers via npm scripts
  - Developer machines running `next dev` with custom prebuild hooks
level: high
(source:windows.sysmon OR source:linux.auditd) @EventID:1 (@ParentImage:(*\node.exe OR *\NODE.EXE) OR @ParentImage:*/node OR @process.parent.executable.name:node) (@Image:(*\cmd.exe OR *\CMD.EXE OR *\powershell.exe OR *\PowerShell.exe OR *\POWERSHELL.EXE OR *\pwsh.exe OR *\PWSH.EXE) OR @Image:(/bin/sh OR /bin/bash OR /usr/bin/sh OR /usr/bin/bash OR /bin/dash OR /bin/zsh) OR @process.executable.name:(sh OR bash OR dash OR zsh)) NOT @ParentCommandLine:(*"next build"* OR *"next dev"*)
#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2 ParentBaseFileName=/^node(\.exe)?$/i ImageFileName=/(\\|\/)(cmd\.exe|powershell\.exe|pwsh\.exe|sh|bash|dash|zsh|ash)$/i
| NOT (ParentCommandLine=/next\s+(build|dev)/i)
| NOT (ParentCommandLine=/(npm|yarn|pnpm)\s+(run|exec)/i)
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, ParentBaseFileName, ImageFileName, CommandLine], function=count())
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count, min(_time) as firstTime, max(_time) as lastTime, values(Processes.process) as cmd, values(Processes.parent_process) as parent_cmd, values(Processes.process_hash) as hash from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("node.exe","node") AND Processes.process_name IN ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","sh","bash","dash","zsh","ash") by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.parent_process_name, Processes.process_name | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | where NOT match(parent_cmd, "next\s+(build|dev)") AND NOT match(user, "\\$$") | `security_content_ctime(firstTime)` | `security_content_ctime(lastTime)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count, min(_time) as firstTime, max(_time) as lastTime, values(Processes.process) as cmd, values(Processes.parent_process) as parent_cmd, values(Processes.process_hash) as hash from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("node.exe","node") AND Processes.process_name IN ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","sh","bash","dash","zsh","ash") by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.parent_process_name, Processes.process_name | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | where NOT match(parent_cmd, "next\s+(build|dev)") AND NOT match(user, "\\$$") | `security_content_ctime(firstTime)` | `security_content_ctime(lastTime)`
[LLM] Anomalous POST to Next.js Server Action / RSC endpoint with 5xx error clustering Exploitation Medium
Targets Snyk's two explicit runtime indicators: 'requests to RSC routes containing malformed or unexpected RSC Flight frames' and 'sudden increases in server function invocation errors'. Surfaces POST traffic carrying the `Next-Action` header or `?_rsc=` / `RSC=1` markers that returns clusters of 5xx responses from a single source IP — the wire-level shape of a crafted-payload probe against the unsafe Flight deserialiser. Rationale: Snyk's own runtime detection guidance names exactly these two signals: malformed RSC Flight frames on RSC routes AND sudden spikes in server function invocation errors. Anchored on the Next.js-specific wire markers `/_next/`, `?_rsc=`, `RSC=1`, and the `Next-Action` request header that the App Router emits for server actions — these are public Next.js conventions, not inferred. 5xx clustering by source IP within a 5m bucket lifts the signal above ordinary error noise (P95 in healthy Next.js is <2 5xx per source IP per 5m). Cross-checked against: • https://snyk.io/blog/security-advisory-critical-rce-vulnerabilities-react-server-components/ • https://nextjs.org/docs/app/building-your-application/data-fetching/server-actions-and-mutations • https://github.com/vercel/next.js/security/advisories
ATT&CKT1190 T1059.007
Data sourcesWeb
// Defender XDR has limited HTTP-server-log telemetry; this pivots on outbound connections initiated by the Node.js process serving RSC after a burst of inbound 5xx (use UC2/UC3-network combo if HTTP logs unavailable).
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("node.exe","node")
| where RemoteIPType == "Public"
| where ActionType == "ConnectionSuccess"
| summarize ConnCount = count(), DistinctRemotes = dcount(RemoteIP), Remotes = make_set(RemoteIP, 20), SampleCmd = any(InitiatingProcessCommandLine) by DeviceName, bin(Timestamp, 5m)
| where DistinctRemotes >= 3 or ConnCount > 20
| order by Timestamp desc
let WindowMin = 5m;
let ErrorThreshold = 10;
union isfuzzy=true
    (AppServiceHTTPLogs
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)
        | where CsMethod == "POST"
        | where (CsUriStem startswith "/_next/" or CsUriQuery has "_rsc=" or CsUriQuery has "RSC=1")
        | where ScStatus >= 500 and ScStatus < 600
        | extend SrcIP = CIp, Host = CsHost, Uri = CsUriStem, Status = ScStatus, Method = CsMethod, UA = UserAgent),
    (W3CIISLog
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)
        | where csMethod == "POST"
        | where (csUriStem startswith "/_next/" or csUriQuery has "_rsc=" or csUriQuery has "RSC=1")
        | where scStatus >= 500 and scStatus < 600
        | extend SrcIP = cIP, Host = sComputerName, Uri = csUriStem, Status = scStatus, Method = csMethod, UA = csUserAgent),
    (CommonSecurityLog
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)
        | where RequestMethod == "POST"
        | where (RequestURL contains "/_next/" or RequestURL contains "_rsc=" or RequestURL contains "RSC=1" or RequestContext has "Next-Action")
        | where toint(EventOutcome) >= 500 and toint(EventOutcome) < 600
        | extend SrcIP = SourceIP, Host = DestinationHostName, Uri = RequestURL, Status = toint(EventOutcome), Method = RequestMethod, UA = RequestClientApplication)
| summarize ErrorCount = count(), DistinctUris = dcount(Uri), SampleUris = make_set(Uri, 10), SampleUA = any(UA) by SrcIP, Host, bin(TimeGenerated, WindowMin)
| where ErrorCount >= ErrorThreshold     // empirical — clean Next.js apps emit <2 5xx/5m per source IP
| order by ErrorCount desc
(source:azure.app_services OR source:nginx OR source:apache OR source:cloudflare OR source:aws.alb) @http.method:POST (@http.url_details.path:*\/_next\/* OR @http.url_details.queryString:(*_rsc=* OR *RSC=1*) OR @http.headers.Next-Action:*) @http.status_code:[500 TO 599]
#event_simpleName=NetworkConnectIP4 ContextImageFileName=/(\\|\/)node(\.exe)?$/i ConnectionDirection=1 RemotePort=*
| LocalPort=/^(3000|3001|8080|8000|80|443)$/
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, ContextImageFileName, LocalPort, RemoteAddressIP4], function=count())
| _count > 5
WEB
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count, dc(Web.uri_path) as distinct_uris, values(Web.http_user_agent) as user_agents, values(Web.uri_path) as uris, values(Web.status) as statuses from datamodel=Web where Web.http_method=POST AND (Web.uri_query="*_rsc=*" OR Web.uri_query="*RSC=1*" OR Web.uri_path="*/_next/*" OR Web.http_header="*Next-Action*") AND Web.status>=500 AND Web.status<600 by Web.src, Web.dest, _time span=5m | `drop_dm_object_name(Web)` | where count >= 10 | sort - count
| tstats summariesonly=false count, dc(Web.uri_path) as distinct_uris, values(Web.http_user_agent) as user_agents, values(Web.uri_path) as uris, values(Web.status) as statuses from datamodel=Web where Web.http_method=POST AND (Web.uri_query="*_rsc=*" OR Web.uri_query="*RSC=1*" OR Web.uri_path="*/_next/*" OR Web.http_header="*Next-Action*") AND Web.status>=500 AND Web.status<600 by Web.src, Web.dest, _time span=5m | `drop_dm_object_name(Web)` | where count >= 10 | sort - count
Asset exposure — vulnerability matches article CVE(s) Reconnaissance High
Match vulnerability scanner output to the CVE(s) named in the article.
ATT&CKT1190
Data sourcesVulnerabilities DeviceInfo DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
// TVM tables are daily snapshots — pin a 1-day window so the engine
// partitions on Timestamp instead of scanning the full retention.
DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where CveId in~ ("CVE-2025-55182", "CVE-2025-66478")
| join kind=inner (DeviceInfo | where Timestamp > ago(1d)) on DeviceId
| project DeviceName, OSPlatform, CveId, VulnerabilitySeverityLevel, RecommendedSecurityUpdate
| order by VulnerabilitySeverityLevel asc, DeviceName asc

// Sentinel has no native TVM table. If MDE→Sentinel streaming is enabled,
// `DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities` is available. Otherwise this UC has
// no Sentinel translation — track via Update / Heartbeat OS-version
// gaps as a coarse approximation.
DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)
| where CveId in~ ("CVE-2025-55182", "CVE-2025-66478")
| join kind=inner (DeviceInfo | where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)) on DeviceId
| project DeviceName, OSPlatform, CveId,
          VulnerabilitySeverityLevel, RecommendedSecurityUpdate
| order by VulnerabilitySeverityLevel asc, DeviceName asc
APPLICATION
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Vulnerabilities
    where Vulnerabilities.signature IN ("CVE-2025-55182", "CVE-2025-66478")
    by Vulnerabilities.dest, Vulnerabilities.signature, Vulnerabilities.severity, Vulnerabilities.cve
| `drop_dm_object_name(Vulnerabilities)`
| sort - severity
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Vulnerabilities
    where Vulnerabilities.signature IN ("CVE-2025-55182", "CVE-2025-66478")
    by Vulnerabilities.dest, Vulnerabilities.signature, Vulnerabilities.severity, Vulnerabilities.cve
| `drop_dm_object_name(Vulnerabilities)`
| sort - severity

ImNetworkSession

Auto-generated hunt targeting the specific binaries, paths, registry locations and command-line fragments named in this article. Hunting tier — needs analyst review and environment tuning before promotion to alerting.
ATT&CKT1204.002
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes Endpoint.Filesystem Endpoint.Registry
// Article-specific bespoke detection — Security Advisory: Critical RCE Vulnerabilities in React Server Components (CVE-
// Hunts the actual binaries / paths / commandline fragments named
// in the article instead of a generic technique-class template.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where (FileName in~ ("next.js"))
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName,
          FolderPath, ProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine
| order by Timestamp desc

// File-creation events for the named binaries / paths
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where ActionType in ("FileCreated","FileModified")
| where (FileName in~ ("next.js"))
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FolderPath,
          FileName, ActionType, InitiatingProcessFileName,
          InitiatingProcessCommandLine
| order by Timestamp desc
ENDPOINT
